# `memory` operations

The exact fields each `memory.*` operation takes and returns.

<!-- Generated by `python scripts/codegen/docs_reference.py` from the op registry; edit the models, not this page. -->

Every op is `POST /v1/<op>` over HTTP and the MCP tool `loom_<op>`. The identity fields (`org`, `namespace`, `agent`, `user_id`, `session_id`) are filled from the token and the MCP session when a transport can; see [identities and namespaces](../../concepts/identities-and-namespaces.md). The [operations index](../operations.md) explains role, kind and the MCP `all` listing. Unknown input fields are served and named in `ignored_args`.

<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->

## `memory.agents_list`

Distinct agent names that have ever written into (org, namespace). agent + user_id are forced sentinels — we aggregate ACROSS them to discover which agents exist.

`POST /v1/memory.agents_list` · MCP `loom_memory_agents_list` · role `viewer` · read

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agents` | `list[str]` | Distinct agent names with a live embedding row in the namespace, sorted. |

## `memory.aggregate`

Templated SQL aggregation over typed records in loom.memory.

`POST /v1/memory.aggregate` · MCP `loom_memory_aggregate` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | required | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `agg_func` | `Literal['count', 'sum', 'avg', 'min', 'max']` | `'count'` | Aggregate to compute: count (rows), or sum / avg / min / max of `agg_field`. |
| `agg_field` | `str` | `'*'` | Field within value JSON to aggregate. |
| `group_by` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Up to 3 value JSON field names to group by; empty = one row over all matches. |
| `filter` | `dict[str, str]` | *(computed)* | Equality filter on JSON-extracted string fields; the identity tuple is always ANDed in. |
| `limit` | `int` | `100` | SQL also hardcodes a LIMIT 1000 floor |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` | `list[_AggregateRow]` | One row per group (a single row when `group_by` is empty). |
| `sql_executed` | `str` | the exact SQL run, for debugging without trace logs |

## `memory.apply`

One scope grammar for every write that can touch more than one row.

`POST /v1/memory.apply` · MCP `loom_memory_apply` · role `writer` · write · audited

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | required | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `target` | `ApplyTarget` | required | Which rows: exactly one of `keys` (up to 500), `filter` (predicates, ANDed) or `search` (a query, optional `min_score`). |
| `action` | `Literal['delete', 'expire', 'lock', 'label', 'demote']` | required | What to do to each row; every action but `delete` needs its block below. |
| `reason` | `str` | required | Why (1..512 chars, and for `expire` not starting with `blacklist.sweep:`); stored as lock_reason / expire_reason where the action has such a column. |
| `limit` | `int \| None` | `None` | Row cap for a `filter` or `search` target, where it is required; unused for `keys`. |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | `True` | True (the default) reports `would_apply` rows without writing; false writes. |
| `expire` | `ApplyExpire \| None` | `None` | For `expire`: `ttl_seconds` or `until`, and an optional `on_expire`. |
| `lock` | `ApplyLock \| None` | `None` | For `lock`: `mode` (`read_only` / `no_delete`), optional `until` / `ttl_seconds`. |
| `label` | `ApplyLabel \| None` | `None` | For `label`: the `tags` and the `mode` — `add`, `replace` or `remove`. |
| `demote` | `ApplyDemote \| None` | `None` | For `demote`: `confidence_delta` or `confidence_factor`; the result is clamped to [`floor`, 1]. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `str` | Echo of the request's action. |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | Echo of the request's `dry_run`. |
| `target` | `str` | keys \| filter \| search |
| `matched` | `int` | Rows the target resolved to; a key with no live row is not counted. |
| `applied` | `int` | rows written (0 under dry_run) |
| `would_apply` | `int` | rows that would be written (dry_run) |
| `refused` | `int` | locks, policy, preconditions |
| `noop` | `int` | Rows already in the asked state: nothing was written for them. |
| `failed` | `int` | Rows whose write raised; each row's `detail` says why. |
| `truncated` | `bool` | more of the caller's rows may match than `limit` |
| `rows` | `list[ApplyRow]` | One entry per matched row: its identity, status, new version and detail. |

## `memory.ask`

Ask a question and get a grounded answer synthesized from the caller's recalled memories (or, with allow_synthesis=False, just the memories).

`POST /v1/memory.ask` · MCP `loom_memory_ask` · role `viewer` · read

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'*'` | Read ALL agents in the accessible namespaces by default (membership is the read boundary; agent is authorship metadata), matching memory.search, and serve every bot's promoted rules. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `query` | `str` | required | The question to answer from the caller's memories (1 to 2000 chars). |
| `memory_type` | `Literal['semantic', 'procedural', 'preference', 'reflection', 'decision'] \| None` | `None` | Same semantics as memory.search: None = facts (reflections excluded); "reflection" = ask over past runs' process lessons only. |
| `tags` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | The same tag predicate memory.search applies, on the candidate read this ask synthesizes from — hard OR-filter by default (`hasAny(tags, …)`), a rank boost of `tag_boost` under `tags_soft`. |
| `tags_soft` | `bool` | `False` | True turns `tags` into a rank boost of `tag_boost` instead of a hard filter. |
| `tag_boost` | `float \| None` | `None` | Forwarded only when set (None = memory.search's own default, 0.3). |
| `top_k` | `int` | `15` | 15: a recency-aware synthesis eval on an autonomous-agent recall workload scored k=15 (with dated, trust-most-recent synthesis) at 57% vs 50% at k=8 — the extra candidates give the synthesizer the fresh fact even when stale cross-session… |
| `bodies` | `Literal['full', 'excerpt', 'none', 'unit', 'source'] \| None` | `None` | Body mode of the retrieval leg: None keeps the deployment default; "source" serves each fact hit its linked evidence passage (or an N-character capsule with `source_span_chars`) so the reader sees the turn or trace the fact came from. |
| `body_budget_tokens` | `int \| None` | `None` | Token budget for whole bodies on the retrieval leg; None = the memory.search default. |
| `source_span_chars` | `int` | `0` | bodies="source": 0 serves the whole linked passage, N an N-character window around the extracted span. |
| `allow_synthesis` | `bool` | `True` | False = retrieval_only: return the memories and let the agent synthesize (parity with code.ask's synthesize=False). |
| `reinforce` | `bool` | `True` | An evaluation read. |
| `reinforcement_weight` | `float \| None` | `None` | Per-request override of the decayed-reinforcement rank weight (None → server default), forwarded to the retrieval legs. |
| `max_answer_chars` | `int` | `0` | Cap the synthesized answer length. 0 = unbounded (default). |
| `namespace_scope` | `Literal['this', 'all_mine'] \| None` | `None` | Pass-through search controls, defaulting exactly as memory.search does: None takes the deployment default `memory_search_default_namespace_scope`, so an unscoped ask reads the same namespaces an unscoped search does. |
| `search_mode` | `Literal['semantic', 'lexical', 'hybrid', 'bm25_hybrid', 'related', 'graph', 'rrf', 'temporal']` | `'rrf'` | Retrieval fusion mode, as memory.search takes it; forwarded only when set on the request, otherwise the search's own default applies. |
| `read_scope` | `Literal['namespace', 'own_user', 'own_session']` | `'namespace'` | Same semantics as memory.search.read_scope; binds to this op's user_id / session_id identity fields. |
| `sensitivity_penalty` | `float \| None` | `None` | Forwarded to memory.search unchanged: None = deployment default demotion of `sensitivity:*`-tagged rows, zeroed on contact intent. |
| `summary_cap` | `int \| None` | `None` | Digest rows admitted to the synthesis window; None = the deployment setting, 0 = unbounded. |
| `rrf_adaptive_lexical` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Forwarded to memory.search only when pinned. |
| `personalization` | `Literal['full', 'none']` | `'full'` | Same semantics as memory.search.personalization; the retrieval leg of an ask runs with it so the answer can be compared with and without priors. |
| `as_of` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | As-of temporal anchor. |
| `as_of_basis` | `Literal['valid_time', 'knowledge_time']` | `'valid_time'` | Which time axis `as_of` replays: "valid_time" (default) = state true as of the anchor; "knowledge_time" = only what loom had learned by the anchor (created_at cutoff, incremental-ingest knowledge-cutoff semantics). |
| `include_superseded` | `bool` | `False` | Forwarded to the retrieval leg; the retired rows then stay in the synthesis window, each line labelled `[superseded <date>; replaced by <key>]`, so the answer can say what a value was before and what replaced it. |
| `precedents` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Precedent reuse: serve the earlier synthesized answer to this question+shape when the synthesis window is byte-identical (same keys, same content hashes) to the one it was written from; no LLM call. |
| `llm_cache` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Exact-prompt LLM response cache: every synthesis-path call is read from loom.llm_response_cache by the sha256 of its full prompt before the provider is called. |
| `depth` | `Literal['auto', 'excerpt', 'raw']` | `'auto'` | Reading depth. "excerpt" answers from fact excerpts only (the default behaviour). "raw" also opens the source turns behind the most relevant facts (one selection call, a bounded evidence read, one more synthesis) on every call. "auto"… |
| `deep_select` | `Literal['llm', 'top'] \| None` | `None` | How the raw read chooses what to open: "llm" (one selection call over the pool) or "top" (the top-ranked memories, no LLM — a deterministic descent from the ranked facts to their source turns). |
| `deep_first` | `bool \| None` | `None` | When the deep pass is known upfront, synthesize once with the raw turns (None/True) or run the excerpt synthesis beside the selector, then the deep one (False). |
| `recount` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Server-side recount of a COUNT answer. |
| `token_budget` | `int \| None` | `None` | Input budget for the synthesis window, in estimated tokens (at the prose rate). |
| `personalize` | `bool \| None` | `None` | A recommendation-shaped question ("can you suggest…", "what should I…") is answered from the user's recorded preferences, tools and constraints first, then tailored. |
| `window_rel_floor` | `float \| None` | `None` | LLM-free window cut: keep synthesis rows whose cosine is >= this fraction of the best row's (e.g. 0.75), never fewer than LOOM_MEMORY_ASK_RELEVANCE_GATE_MIN_KEEP rows. |
| `decompose` | `Literal['', 'off', 'auto', 'always']` | `''` | Question decomposition: "" or "off" = none; "always" splits this question into 2-4 sub-questions (the cheap tier) and retrieves each; "auto" does so only on multi-hop or date-of-event cues. |
| `world_knowledge` | `Literal['', 'forbid', 'allow']` | `''` | General-knowledge bridging: "" = the server setting (LOOM_MEMORY_ASK_WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, default forbid); "allow" lets the synthesizer combine a memory fact with public knowledge, marking the sentences that did (output `grounding` =… |
| `consistency` | `Literal['', 'inline', 'deferred']` | `''` | When the answer-vs-citation judge runs. "" = the server setting (LOOM_MEMORY_ASK_CONSISTENCY_MODE, default inline); "inline" awaits it and rides the verdict on the wire; "deferred" answers first — the wire fields stay empty and the… |
| `route_prior` | `str` | `''` | The verdict prior for the cheap-vs-strong router. "" = the server setting (LOOM_MEMORY_ASK_SYNTH_ROUTE_PRIOR, default off); "off" forces the rule-only router; "measured" the shipped table; or a JSON object of route -> contradicted rate. |
| `route_prior_max_cheap` | `float \| None` | `None` | Contradiction rate at or under which a strong-routed ask goes cheap; None = the deployment setting. |
| `mid_model` | `str` | `''` | The mid synthesis tier, pinned per request. |
| `mid_routes` | `str` | `''` | Which routes use the mid tier: "" = the setting, "off", "uncertain" or a comma list of route reason tokens. |
| `default_answer_chars` | `int \| None` | `None` | The deployment default for the answer length, pinned per request. |
| `digest_descent` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Search-side digest descent for this call (None = on, False = off). |
| `presupposition_rule` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Presupposition check in the synthesizer (None = on; False turns it off). |
| `set_window` | `int \| None` | `None` | Synthesis window for set questions (None = setting, 0 = off). |
| `knowledge` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Also read the knowledge plane (None = setting). |
| `recent_messages` | `list[_RecentMessage]` | *(computed)* | The turns the question sits in, supplied by the caller and never stored — rendered as a RECENT TURNS block above the evidence so "and what did she say about that?" resolves against the turn above it. |
| `observation_date` | `str` | `''` | The question's own date (ISO yyyy-mm-dd), as memory.search takes it: "two months ago" resolves against it, for retrieval's date anchors and for the synthesizer's note. |
| `gh_items_fallback` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Answer from loom's GitHub-items index when retrieval abstains on a question naming a PR/issue number. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `answer` | `str` | The synthesized answer; empty when the ask abstained or ran retrieval_only. |
| `source` | `Literal['synthesized', 'retrieval_only', 'abstained', 'record', 'precedent']` | "record": answered from an exact record (the GitHub-items index or the tracker) instead of LLM synthesis. "precedent": the earlier synthesized answer to this question+shape, served because its evidence is byte-identical. |
| `abstain` | `bool` | True when retrieval abstained and no record answered: `answer` is empty. |
| `abstain_reason` | `str` | Carries the retrieval abstain reason, or "budget_capped" when synthesis was skipped because the namespace is over its cost cap. |
| `memory_keys` | `list[str]` | Citations: the memory_keys the answer drew on (all recalled keys in retrieval_only mode). |
| `results` | `list[_MemorySearchHit]` | The raw retrieved memories, so callers still see the sources. |
| `cited_sessions` | `list[str]` | The sessions the cited memories were written under: the `session_id` of every hit in `results` whose key is in `memory_keys`, first-cited order, no repeats, "" skipped. |
| `next` | `str` | Protocol nudge, set only when the call carried a run_id (see MemorySearchOutput.next). |
| `synth_model` | `str` | Synthesis routing (two-tier cascade, LOOM_MEMORY_ASK_SYNTH_MODEL_CHEAP). |
| `route_tier` | `Literal['', 'cheap', 'mid', 'strong']` | The synthesis tier that answered: cheap, mid or strong; empty when nothing was synthesized. |
| `route_reason` | `str` | The routing rule that chose `route_tier` ("single_tier" when the cascade is off); empty when nothing was synthesized. |
| `llm_cache_hits` | `int` | How many of this ask's LLM calls the exact-prompt response cache served (no provider call, nothing spent) and how many went to the provider. |
| `llm_cache_misses` | `int` | LLM calls this ask sent to the provider past the response cache. |
| `llm_cache` | `bool` | Whether the cache wrapped this ask at all — the request pin, the traffic class's policy or the deployment default, whichever applied — and the dollars the hits did not spend at the price table (the stored token counts of the served rows). |
| `llm_cache_saved_usd` | `float` | Dollars the cache hits did not spend, at the price table. |
| `temporal_consistency` | `float \| None` | What the answer cited, scored without a model call (`cited_sessions` above is the list these are computed on). temporal_consistency: mean window score of the cited rows' dates against the question's bounded window (None = no window / no… |
| `citation_concentration` | `float \| None` | 1 / distinct cited sessions; None when nothing was cited. |
| `escalated` | `bool` | True when the cheap-tier answer failed its check and was redone on a stronger tier. |
| `gate_mode` | `str` | Similarity-knee telemetry (`window_rel_floor`). gate_mode is "" when the cut was off or skipped, else knee \| floor \| kept_all; the counts say how many window rows the synthesizer actually read vs. dropped. |
| `gate_kept` | `int` | Window rows the synthesizer read after the similarity-knee cut. |
| `gate_dropped` | `int` | Window rows the similarity-knee cut removed. |
| `pending_extraction` | `int` | Deferred batches not yet extracted in scope; see MemorySearchOutput.pending_extraction. |
| `pending_evidence` | `int` | Raw turns of those pending batches that were read into the synthesis window because they spoke to the question. > 0 says the answer used evidence no memory row carries yet. |
| `retrieval_query` | `str` | The text retrieval actually embedded when the query carried an answer scaffold (option block, "reply with the letter", stamped date) that was split off for the synthesizer. |
| `facets` | `list[str]` | Facet completion: on a count question, the attribute facets pulled (`age`, `location`) and how many in-scope memories they added to the synthesis window beyond similarity retrieval. |
| `facet_memories_added` | `int` | In-scope memories the facet pull added to the window beyond similarity retrieval; 0 when it did not run. |
| `consistency` | `Literal['', 'entailed', 'neutral', 'contradicted']` | Answer-vs-citation audit (LOOM_MEMORY_ASK_CONSISTENCY_CHECK): does the answer say what its cited memories say? "entailed" / "neutral" / "contradicted", "" when the check did not run. consistency_score is (1 + P_entail - P_contradict) / 2.… |
| `consistency_score` | `float` | (1 + P_entail - P_contradict) / 2, 0 to 1; 0 when the check did not run. |
| `consistency_note` | `str` | The cited memory and phrase a contradiction turns on; empty otherwise. |
| `identifier_chase_hops` | `int` | Identifier chase: hops walked from the question's identifiers through the identifiers the reached memories name, and the memories those hops added to the window. 0 / 0 when the question named no identifier or the reached memories named… |
| `identifier_chase_added` | `int` | Memories the identifier-chase hops added to the window. |
| `premise_conflict` | `str` | The question's premise checked against PINNED or human-VERIFIED memories in the window (LOOM_MEMORY_ASK_PREMISE_CHECK). |
| `premise_note` | `str` | One line naming the presupposition and what the trusted memory records; empty when no conflict was found. |
| `premise_verdict` | `str` | The synthesizer's premise verdict (supported / unsupported / ""). |
| `attribution_note` | `str` | "fired" when the computed attribution note rode the synthesis call, "" otherwise. |
| `depth` | `Literal['', 'excerpt', 'raw']` | Reading depth that produced the answer: "excerpt" = fact excerpts only, "raw" = the source turns behind the selected facts were opened too. |
| `deep_fired` | `bool` | True when the deep-evidence pass ran (see `deep_reason`), even if it opened no source text. |
| `decomposed` | `list[str]` | The sub-questions retrieved on their own; empty when the question was retrieved whole. |
| `decomposed_parts` | `int` | How many sub-questions that was (0 = retrieved whole). |
| `superseded_dropped` | `int` | Superseded rows taken out of the synthesis pool; 0 under `include_superseded`. |
| `stale_sentences_masked` | `int` | Sentences in chunks and summaries masked because they restate a superseded row. |
| `entity_followed` | `list[str]` | Bridge entities the second hop followed. |
| `when_evidence_turns` | `int` | Dated raw turns the second synthesis read (0 = no fallback). |
| `decompose_failed` | `int` | Sub-question retrievals that raised and were skipped (fail-open), and the widened pool the retrieval ran with (0 = the caller's top_k). |
| `pool_k` | `int` | The widened candidate pool retrieval ran with; 0 = the caller's `top_k`. |
| `grounding` | `Literal['', 'memory', 'mixed']` | "memory": every sentence came from the memories; "mixed": the answer bridged with general knowledge under world_knowledge="allow" and marked those sentences; "": no synthesis ran. |
| `deep_reason` | `str` | Why the raw read ran: "requested" (depth="raw") or "temporal"; empty when it did not. |
| `deep_keys` | `list[str]` | The memory keys whose source turns the raw read opened. |
| `deep_chars` | `int` | Characters of source text the raw read handed the synthesizer. |
| `code_hits` | `int` | Code-plane grounding rows the synthesizer saw. |
| `pool_facts` | `int` | Fact rows and verbatim chunk rows the synthesizer saw. |
| `pool_chunks` | `int` | Verbatim chunk rows the synthesizer saw. |
| `prompt_blocks` | `dict[str, int]` | Estimated tokens per block of the synthesis prompt — system, notes, window (fact and summary rows), chunks, code, chase, knowledge, raw_turns, timeline, recent, scratchpad, elision, graph, question, other (heads and separators) — summed… |
| `deep_selector` | `Literal['', 'llm', 'top']` | Which selector chose the opened memories: "llm" or "top" ("" when the raw read did not run). |
| `deep_first` | `Literal['', 'single', 'empty_block', 'deep_failed']` | How the deep-first order resolved. "single" = one synthesis with the raw turns (no excerpt synthesis ran); "empty_block" = the raw block was empty so the excerpt synthesis ran alone; "deep_failed" = the deep answer failed the citation… |
| `synth_calls` | `int` | How many synthesis-family calls the ask made (primary, deep, escalation, fallbacks; 0 when nothing was synthesized). |
| `synth_input_tokens` | `int` | The provider-side accounting of the model that answered (`synth_model`) over this ask: its calls, whole-prompt input tokens, the share the provider served from its prompt cache and the share it wrote to it, and its dollars at the price… |
| `synth_cached_input_tokens` | `int` | Input tokens of the answering model the provider served from its prompt cache. |
| `synth_cache_write_tokens` | `int` | Input tokens of the answering model the provider wrote to its prompt cache. |
| `synth_cost_usd` | `float` | Dollars the answering model's calls cost at the price table, cache rates applied. |
| `context_tokens_est` | `int` | Estimated input tokens of the memories the synthesizer saw, and how many ranked memories `token_budget` cut from the window (0 when no budget). |
| `context_trimmed` | `int` | Ranked memories `token_budget` cut from the window; 0 when no budget. |
| `summary_hits` | `int` | Session-summary hits that survived into the synthesis window. |
| `knowledge_hits` | `int` | Knowledge passages the synthesizer was shown. |
| `timeline_rows` | `int` | Dated memories rendered in the computed timeline; 0 = none. |
| `count_recomputed` | `bool` | A COUNT answer whose number was rewritten from the model's own ITEMS verdicts. |

## `memory.assign_category`

Link a memory to one of the namespace's registered categories.

`POST /v1/memory.assign_category` · MCP `loom_memory_assign_category` · role `writer` · idempotent · audited · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | required | The memory to categorise; the key is stored as given, not checked for a live row. |
| `category_name` | `str` | required | A category registered in the namespace (namespace.register_category), else 404. |
| `tombstone` | `bool` | `False` | True rescinds the memory's link to the category. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `assigned` | `bool` | True when the link was written; False when it was rescinded. |
| `category_id` | `str` | The id of the named category. |

## `memory.auto_retirements`

The memories Loom retired on its own (the conflict resolver, `newest_wins`), newest record first, inside the request's read scope.

`POST /v1/memory.auto_retirements` · MCP `loom_memory_auto_retirements` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |

## `memory.bulk_set`

Insert many memory entries in one batched CH insert.

`POST /v1/memory.bulk_set` · MCP `loom_memory_bulk_set` · role `writer` · idempotent · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | required | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `entries` | `list[_BulkSetEntry]` | required | The entries to write, each with its own key, value and per-entry fields; all share the caller's identity. |
| `contextualize` | `bool` | `False` | Treat this call's entries as one document and prepend a model-written one-line context to what each entry EMBEDS and to its content_excerpt (value untouched). |
| `detect_updates` | `bool \| None` | `None` | See MemorySetFromMessagesInput.detect_updates (same semantics). |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `written` | `list[_BulkSetResult]` | One result per entry, in order: key, version (0 when not inserted) and verdict. |
| `skipped_pinned` | `list[str]` | Keys whose live row is pinned: skipped (result version=0) rather than overwritten, since overwriting would also unpin (entries default pinned=False). |
| `skipped_locked` | `list[str]` | Keys whose live row is locked read_only: skipped (result version=0), where memory.set would answer 423 LOCKED. |
| `skipped_blacklisted` | `list[str]` | Keys whose entry the blacklist refused: not written (result version=0), where memory.set would answer 422 BLACKLISTED. |
| `merged` | `list[str]` | Conflict verdicts, the same four memory.set produces: canonical restatement of an existing row → not inserted, existing row reinforced; close to a pinned peer → not inserted; same fact in other words → inserted as status=duplicate… |
| `value_updates_linked` | `int` | Older rows marked superseded by a value update in this batch. |
| `rejected_pinned` | `list[str]` | Keys not inserted because they are too close to a pinned row. |
| `duplicates` | `list[str]` | Keys inserted as `status=duplicate`: the same fact as a live row in other words. |
| `conflicted` | `list[str]` | Keys inserted and cross-linked as `status=conflicted` with the rows they contradict. |
| `unchecked` | `int` | Entries past bulk_conflict_check_max_entries, written without a check. |
| `retyped` | `list[str]` | Entries declared procedural whose value is not a procedure body, stored as semantic tagged retyped_from:procedural. |
| `identity_duplicates` | `dict[str, str]` | Entries not written because a live row in the same identity already carries the same content: entry key -> the keeper's key. |
| `stage_ms` | `dict[str, float]` | Wall time per phase of the write (existing_lookup, entity_resolution, prepare, embed, verdicts, insert, value_updates, projections, total) — Diagnostic; readers tolerate unknown keys. |

## `memory.consolidate`

Periodic consolidation pass — merges fragmented memories about the same subject that slip past hash-dedup and extraction-time dedup.

`POST /v1/memory.consolidate` · MCP `loom_memory_consolidate` · role `writer` · write · audited

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | required | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `limit` | `int` | `200` | At most this many of the identity's newest eligible rows are clustered. |
| `similarity_threshold` | `float` | `0.85` | Cosine at which two rows may cluster; they also need a shared entity unless the cosine reaches max(threshold + 0.05, 0.92). |
| `min_age_seconds` | `int` | `3600` | Skip memories newer than this — protects in-flight writes from being consolidated away before retrieval can use them. |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | `False` | True still runs the merge LLM calls but writes nothing: no canonical row, no tombstones. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `consolidated` | `list[MemoryConsolidateResult]` | One entry per cluster merged (or that would be, under `dry_run`). |
| `examined` | `int` | Eligible rows read: live, unpinned, unlocked, embedded, older than `min_age_seconds`, and neither labelled `high` nor reading as `high` (never sent to the merge model). |
| `clusters_found` | `int` | Clusters of two or more rows found. |
| `clusters_failed` | `int` | Clusters whose merge LLM call failed or returned an unparseable / incomplete JSON object. |
| `clusters_refused_lossy` | `int` | Of the failed clusters, those the merge guard refused because the merged text lost a date, quantity, identifier, name or negation one source carried; the sources stay as they were. |
| `skipped_in_flight` | `int` | Always 0: rows newer than `min_age_seconds` are left out of the read, not counted. |
| `tokens_in` | `int` | Prompt tokens of the merge LLM calls. |
| `tokens_out` | `int` | Completion tokens of the merge LLM calls. |

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |

| `orphans` | `int` | ... whose canonical is gone: memory.resolve_orphan_duplicates re-activates them. |

| `sample` | `list[_DedupCollapsePair]` | Up to `sample` pairs whose canonical is live, as duplicate → canonical keys. |

## `memory.demonstrate`

Test-time learning from memory: the nearest memories tagged as examples (default tag `example`, label carried as `label:<value>`), a similarity-weighted vote over their labels, the predicted label…

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'*'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `query` | `str` | required | The input to classify; the example memories nearest to it are retrieved. |
| `k` | `int` | `8` | At most this many labelled examples feed the vote and the block, 1-50. |
| `example_tag` | `str` | `'example'` | Only memories carrying this tag are examples. |

| `namespace_scope` | `Literal['this', 'all_mine']` | `'this'` | `this` searches `namespace`; `all_mine` also the caller's own namespaces (up to the fan-out cap), but labels are read from `namespace` only. |
| `min_margin` | `float` | `0.0` | Below this normalised top-vote margin the prediction is reported but `abstain` is set, so a caller can fall back to its own reasoning. |
| `max_block_chars` | `int` | `6000` | Character budget of `few_shot_block`; the nearest example is always included. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | `str` | The query, echoed. |
| `demonstrations` | `list[DemonstrationRow]` | The labelled examples used, nearest first, at most `k`. |
| `votes` | `dict[str, float]` | label -> normalised similarity-weighted vote (sums to 1 when any) |
| `predicted_label` | `str` | The label with the largest vote; "" when no labelled example was found. |
| `margin` | `float` | The top vote minus the runner-up (votes sum to 1); 1.0 when only one label voted. |
| `abstain` | `bool` | True when no labelled example was found or `margin` is below `min_margin`; the prediction is still returned. |
| `abstain_reason` | `str` | `no_examples`, `no_labelled_examples` or `low_margin`; "" when not abstaining. |
| `few_shot_block` | `str` | The examples as `Input:` / `Label:` pairs for a prompt, nearest first, within `max_block_chars`. |
| `examined` | `int` | How many nearest memories were examined and how many carried a label. |
| `labelled` | `int` | How many of them carried a label (the demonstrations used, at most `k`). |

`POST /v1/memory.for_file` · MCP `loom_memory_for_file` · role `viewer` · read

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |

| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |

| `tags` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Optional tag filter (any-of), e.g. ["project:loom"] under the plugin's tag-scoped project mode. |
| `top_k` | `int` | `8` | At most this many rows, across every namespace read. |
| `token_budget` | `int` | `300` | Cap on the rendered block, which its header, removal footer and "… more" line can exceed; the hook injects `rendered` verbatim. |
| `include_conflicted` | `bool` | `True` | Conflicted rows are still live facts a reader should see; duplicates, superseded and rejected rows are not. |

| `rendered` | `str` | Prompt-ready block, cut at token_budget. |
| `tokens_estimate` | `int` | Size of `rendered` at 4 chars per token; 0 when it is empty. |

## `memory.get`

WHAT: Fetch one memory by exact `memory_key`.

`POST /v1/memory.get` · MCP `loom_memory_get` · role `viewer` · read

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | required | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | required | The key to read: tried under this identity, then the same user's row under any agent. |
| `if_version` | `int \| None` | `None` | Version precondition: the version the caller already holds. |
| `include_recall_breakdown` | `bool` | `False` | Opt-in per-agent recall breakdown; off by default to keep get cheap. |
| `as_of` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | As-of replay filter: restrict to rows with coalesce(valid_at, created_at) <= as_of. |
| `fields` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | A whitelist of output field names (`value`, `tags`, `status`, `memory_type`, `recall_count`, `created_at`, …). |
| `follow` | `bool` | `False` | Serve the live canonical a `status='duplicate'` row points to (its `duplicate_of`, same org and namespace, up to three hops) instead of the exact row; the response then carries `resolved_from` = the key asked for and `canonical_key` = the… |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `found` | `bool` | False when no live, unexpired row of this user holds the key. |
| `unchanged` | `bool` | True when `if_version` matched the live row: version below, no body. |
| `memory_id` | `str` | Stable row id, surfaced so a key-recalled row can record an outcome without a second lookup. |
| `value` | `dict[str, Any] \| list[Any] \| str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` | The stored value as written (text, object, list or scalar). |
| `memory_type` | `str \| None` | The row's memory type; None when not found. |
| `confidence` | `float \| None` | The writer's confidence in the fact, 0..1 (a `demote` expiry lowers it). |
| `version` | `int \| None` | Nanosecond version of the live row; send it back as `if_version` to poll. |
| `version_text` | `str \| None` | The same version as a decimal string, exact for a JavaScript caller (the number is above 2^53, which JSON.parse rounds): send this one to memory.delete_version. |
| `created_at` | `datetime \| None` | When the key was first written; kept across later versions. |
| `updated_at` | `datetime \| None` | Last write to this key; distinct from created_at, which is preserved across updates. |
| `expires_at` | `datetime \| None` | When the row expires (memory.get hides it after that, with `as_of` only a high one; memory.list serves it until the expiry sweep, and memory.bulk_get does too, except a high one); None = no expiry. |
| `on_expire` | `str` | Post-action on expiry ('' = tombstone) and its reason. |
| `expire_reason` | `str` | Why the expiry was set, as the writer gave it; '' when none. |
| `valid_at` | `datetime \| None` | Real-world time the fact became true (distinct from created_at = when recorded). |
| `valid_to` | `datetime \| None` | Closing bound of the fact's stated validity ("until 2024"); NULL = open interval, the common case. |
| `temporal_anchor` | `datetime \| None` | Date the fact is ABOUT (distinct from valid_at) and how precisely the source pinned it (0..1 per the extraction rubric; 0 = unscored). |
| `temporal_confidence` | `float` | How precisely the source pinned `temporal_anchor`, 0..1; 0 = unscored. |
| `pinned` | `bool` | True when the row was saved with `memory.pin`: a write that does not pin never replaces it (409 PINNED_CONFLICT). |
| `actor` | `str` | Who wrote the live version (`human:<subject>` / `process:<subject>`) and how the content entered memory (asserted \| extracted \| observed \| derived \| imported \| external). |
| `source_class` | `str` | How the content entered memory: asserted \| extracted \| observed \| derived \| imported \| external; '' when not found. |
| `agent` | `str` | Writer agent of the resolved row. |
| `user_id` | `str` | The resolved row's user and session: a write back to this row (restore, verify) names them, since a key repeats across users and sessions. |
| `session_id` | `str` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `status` | `str \| None` | Lifecycle state from loom.memory.status. |
| `code` | `list[CodeLink]` | The code this memory is linked to: each link's path, symbol, state (`fresh`, `moved`, `changed`, `unresolved` or `missing`) and the `revise` policy's suggestion. |
| `superseded_by` | `str` | For a `status='superseded'` row, the memory_id of the row that replaced it ('' otherwise) — the bundle turns it into a `supersedes` edge on the newer row. |
| `duplicate_of` | `str` | The row this one duplicates (status='duplicate'), and the verdict the row shows on read, derived from `status` (active → clear, conflicted → conflict, duplicate, superseded). |
| `conflict_verdict` | `str` | clear \| conflict \| duplicate \| superseded, as described above. |
| `canonical_key` | `str \| None` | For a `status='duplicate'` row, the memory_key of the canonical that answers for it ("" when that row is no longer active — the orphan case `memory.resolve_orphan_duplicates` repairs). |
| `resolved_from` | `str \| None` | On an answer given by another row, the memory_key the caller asked for: a `follow: true` read that served a duplicate's canonical, or a memory.bulk_get chunk id answered by its parent fact. |
| `tags` | `list[str]` | Surfaced so an in-place tag edit can preserve existing tags/entities rather than clobbering them. |
| `entities` | `list[str]` | Entity names stored on the row (lowercased), internal sentinels left out. |
| `content_sha256` | `str` | SHA-256 of the live value (canonical JSON); pass back as if_match_sha256 for a no-clobber update against the value THIS read saw. |
| `char_limit` | `int \| None` | Server-enforced char cap on `value` (NULL = no cap). |
| `recall_count` | `int` | Recall telemetry from loom.memory_usage_*, bumped by search's auto_touch path. |
| `last_recalled_at` | `datetime \| None` | When a search last served the row; None = never recalled. |
| `verified_by` | `str` | Attestation (memory.verify). |
| `verified_at` | `datetime \| None` | When the attestation in `verified_by` was made; None = never attested, or revoked. |
| `verification` | `str` | human \| process: attested and unchanged since; stale: the content changed after the attestation; none. |
| `lock_mode` | `str` | Lock in force (memory.lock). '' = unlocked or lapsed. |
| `lock_reason` | `str` | Why the lock was set, as the locker gave it; '' when unlocked. |
| `lock_until` | `datetime \| None` | When the lock lapses; None = open-ended, or no lock. |
| `locked_by` | `str` | Who set the lock (`human:<subject>` / `process:<subject>` under auth); '' when unlocked. |
| `recall_by_agent` | `list[_RecallByAgent]` | Per-agent recall breakdown (last 30 days); populated only when include_recall_breakdown=True. |
| `sensitivity` | `str` | '' \| low \| medium \| high. |

| `verification` | `str` | human \| process: attested and unchanged since; stale: the content changed after the attestation; none. |

| `lock_mode` | `str` | Lock in force and expiry post-action. |
| `lock_reason` | `str` | Why the lock was set; '' when unlocked or lapsed. |

| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `silent_after_days` | `int` | `30` | A live row older than this and never recalled is "silent". |
| `top_k` | `int` | `10` | How many entries `top_recalled` lists. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `live` | `int` | Active, untombstoned rows in the namespace, across every agent and user. |
| `recalled_ever` | `int` | Live rows recalled at least once. |
| `used_ever` | `int` | Live rows with at least one reported use. |
| `harmed_ever` | `int` | live rows with at least one harm event |
| `silent` | `int` | live and never recalled |
| `silent_older` | `int` | silent AND older than silent_after_days |
| `silent_share` | `float` | `silent` / `live`, 0..1; 0 when the namespace holds no live row. |
| `silent_after_days` | `int` | Echo of the request's `silent_after_days`. |
| `by_type` | `list[MemoryHealthTypeRow]` | Per memory type: live rows and how many were ever recalled, largest first. |
| `top_recalled` | `list[MemoryHealthTopRow]` | The most recalled live rows (by recall count, then use count), at most `top_k`. |
| `staleness` | `MemoryHealthStaleness` | Age buckets, validity-end, expiry and pin counts, and days since reinforced. |
| `footprint` | `MemoryHealthFootprint` | Summed value length of the live rows and its chars/4 token estimate. |

## `memory.link`

Author an explicit edge between two memories (or two entities).

`POST /v1/memory.link` · MCP `loom_memory_link` · role `writer` · write · audited

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |

| `to_key` | `str` | required | The edge's object endpoint (a memory key or an entity string). |
| `relation` | `str` | `''` | Relation verb, canonicalized on write (memory/domain/edge_relations.py): supports, depends_on, caused, contradicts, refines, implements, validates, supersedes, blocks, fixes, derived_from, related_to. |
| `label` | `str` | `''` | Free-text label stored on the edge and returned by memory.provenance. |

| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The run that asserted the edge (run.begin); joins the edge to its ledger. |
| `weight` | `float` | `1.0` | edge strength; higher = stronger preference at graph-mode rank time |
| `tombstone` | `bool` | `False` | rescind a prior edge (writes a tombstone row) |

| --- | --- | --- |
| `linked` | `bool` | True when an edge was written; False when the call wrote a tombstone. |
| `from_key` | `str` | The written row, echoed so the caller can chain. from/to are the canonical direction (a reversed verb such as blocked_by is flipped). |
| `to_key` | `str` | The edge's object endpoint as stored, after any direction flip. |
| `relation` | `str` | canonical verb as stored |
| `confidence` | `float` | The relationship confidence as stored, echoed. |
| `conflict_opened` | `bool` | relation == contradicts and both endpoints are live memories: both rows are now status='conflicted' and appear in conflicts.list. |
| `relation_defaulted` | `bool` | The caller passed no relation; the row was stored as `related_to`. |

| `memory_type` | `str \| None` | `None` | Only rows of this memory type; None = every type. |

| `include_proposed` | `bool` | `False` | `status='proposed'` rows (facts on trial) are skipped unless asked for; `memory.proposals` lists them with their graded counts. |
| `as_of` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | see MemoryGetInput.as_of |
| `tags` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Only rows carrying any one of these tags, in any case; empty = no tag filter. |
| `tags_every` | `bool` | `False` | Require every one of `tags` instead of any one; default off. |

| `fields` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Whitelist of entry field names; every entry carries only those plus `memory_key` and `sensitivity`. |

| --- | --- | --- |

| `truncated` | `bool` | true if more entries exist beyond `limit` |
| `total` | `int` | Total rows matching this scope (ignores `limit`), so callers can show "N of TOTAL". 0 on an `unchanged` poll, which carries no counts. |
| `today` | `int` | Of `total`, how many were created since UTC midnight today — the true "today" count (not the truncated page count the day-group headers show). |
| `namespace_version` | `str` | The namespace's newest memory version (any agent, any status — every write moves it). |
| `unchanged` | `bool` | True when `known_version` matched: entries, total and today were not read and are their defaults. |
| `hidden` | `int` | When a `prefix` listing is empty, how many rows under the prefix it left out as `duplicate`/`superseded`, and the flag that serves them. 0 / "" otherwise. |
| `hidden_hint` | `str` | A sentence naming those hidden rows and the flag that lists them; '' otherwise. |

Lock one row against a class of writes.

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |

| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |

| `version` | `int \| None` | Nanosecond version of the lock row written; None when not found. |
| `lock_mode` | `str` | The mode now in force (`read_only` / `no_delete`); '' when not found. |
| `lock_until` | `datetime \| None` | When the lock lapses; None = open-ended, or not found. |
| `locked_by` | `str` | Who holds the lock (`human:<subject>` / `process:<subject>` under auth); '' when not found. |
| `previous_mode` | `str` | '' when the row was unlocked before this call |

## `memory.pin`

WHAT: Save a standing fact and protect it.

`POST /v1/memory.pin` · MCP `loom_memory_pin` · role `writer` · idempotent

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | required | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | required | The key to write; a write to a key that already holds a row adds a new version. |
| `memory_type` | `str` | `'semantic'` | Coarse classification axis (drives procedural memory + tag_registry policy lookups). |
| `value` | `dict[str, Any] \| list[Any] \| str \| int \| float \| bool` | required | The fact itself: plain text, or a JSON object, list or scalar. |
| `tags` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Flexible classification, filterable at recall via MemorySearchInput.tags; per-tag retention/dedup/conflict policy via NamespaceRegisterInput.tag_registry. |
| `entities` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Explicit entities for a point write. |
| `relations` | `list[tuple[str, str, str]]` | *(computed)* | The (subject, relation, object) facts the value states, written to the fact graph and linked to the row as a `memory.bulk_set` entry's are: a single-valued fact closes the older one it replaces and, under `newest_wins`, retires the rows… |
| `files` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | The repo files this memory is about (repo-relative path or bare filename); memory.for_file serves it before an edit of them. |
| `confidence` | `float` | `1.0` | The writer's own confidence in the fact, 0..1 (1.0 = certain). |
| `source_trace` | `str` | `''` | Provenance tag of the write (`conversation:<id>`, `curated_doc://…`); a known prefix decides `source_class` (`conversation:` → extracted), and one starting with `memory.delete_version:` is refused. |
| `source_class` | `str \| None` | `None` | Declare that this content came from outside (a tool result, a page, a document): `external`, or `imported`. |
| `source_resource_id` | `str` | `''` | Provenance pointer to the primary source this fact was cited from — a file path, document id, or URL. |
| `ttl_seconds` | `int \| None` | `None` | Expire the row this many seconds from now. |
| `clear_expiry` | `bool` | `False` | Force expires_at=NULL, ignoring per-type/namespace retention defaults. |
| `on_expire` | `Literal['', 'tombstone', 'demote', 'anonymize']` | `''` | What happens when expires_at passes: '' keeps the row's current action (tombstone for a new row); 'demote' clears the expiry and scales confidence down; 'anonymize' replaces the value with a marker and drops the embeddings, keeping the… |
| `expire_reason` | `str` | `''` | Why the expiry is set (at most 512 chars, not starting with `blacklist.sweep:`); '' keeps the row's current reason. |
| `valid_at` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | Real-world time the fact became true (distinct from created_at and from temporal_anchor). |
| `valid_to` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | Closing bound of the fact's stated validity ("until 2024"); NULL = open interval. |
| `pinned` | `bool` | `False` | True when written via memory.pin (explicit-save) |
| `classify` | `bool` | `False` | Call the namespace's classify_endpoint to derive memory_type from `value`. |
| `if_match_sha256` | `str` | `''` | Optimistic-concurrency precondition: 409 PRECONDITION_FAILED if the live row's SHA-256 doesn't match. |
| `char_limit` | `int \| None` | `None` | Server-enforced char cap on the stringified value (422 on exceed). |
| `sensitivity` | `Literal['', 'low', 'medium', 'high']` | `''` | Sensitivity tier. 'high' = never embedded, searched or in a recency pack; read by key only, audited. '' = detect from the value: credentials, card numbers, SSNs, PINs high; email, phone, IBAN medium. |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | `False` | Run the conflict check and return its verdict, peers and `next` WITHOUT writing — no loom.memory row, no embedding row, no audit hash, no usage event, no supersession. |
| `proposed` | `bool` | `False` | Write the fact as a PROPOSAL (`status='proposed'`): not served by default, served to a read that passes `include_proposed`, and accepted or rejected on the graded outcomes of the runs that used it (`run.grade`, `memory.proposals`… |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `int` | nanosecond version assigned by the server |
| `pinned` | `bool` | True when the stored row is pinned: a `memory.pin`, or a restatement of a pinned row. |
| `memory_id` | `str` | UUID assigned to this insert; usable with memory.get_by_id |
| `content_sha256` | `str` | SHA-256 of the just-written value; usable as if_match_sha256 on next write. |
| `status` | `str` | The written row's lifecycle status (`active`, `duplicate`, `proposed`); "" on a write that stored no row (merge, dry run). |
| `duplicate_of` | `str` | Set when this write was tagged status='duplicate': memory_id of the canonical semantically-identical row. |
| `namespace` | `str` | Echoed so a tool-call response carries citable factual data. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | The key the request named; on a `merge` see `merged_into_key`. |
| `merged_into_key` | `str` | On a `merge` the store already held this content under ANOTHER key; nothing was written at `memory_key`, so a get/lock/update of it finds no row. |
| `degraded` | `list[str]` | Providers that fell back on this write and what the response did instead (`classify: caller_type_kept (ReadTimeout)`). |
| `retyped_from` | `str` | Set when the declared memory_type did not fit the value and the row was stored under another type (currently: 'procedural' on a value that is not a procedure body → 'semantic', tagged retyped_from:procedural). |
| `conflict_verdict` | `str` | What the write-time conflict check decided about THIS write — clear \| merge \| duplicate \| conflict \| refines \| rejected (the last only on a dry run; a real write answers 409). |
| `peers` | `list[MemorySetPeer]` | The rows the verdict was reached against (closest first, at most five): the key is the handle for memory.update, the excerpt what the store holds. |
| `next` | `str` | A short machine hint naming the op to reach for: memory.update(key) on a conflict, memory.pin on a merge the store has seen before, "" otherwise. |
| `noop` | `bool` | True when this call wrote nothing: a `merge` (the store already held the fact; its row was reinforced instead) or a dry run. |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | Echo of the request's dry_run so a tool-call transcript is unambiguous. |
| `advisories` | `list[str]` | One line per thing the server noticed about the VALUE that the agent should fix on its side — currently only "base64-encoded". |
| `chunks_written` | `int` | Verbatim chunk rows this write added to the chunk plane for a long searchable value (0 for a short value, a non-searchable type, a merge or a dry run). |

## `memory.recall`

Search the raw conversation turns behind this namespace's memories — the messages `memory.set_from_messages` extracted from — by text and by time.

`POST /v1/memory.recall` · MCP `loom_memory_recall` · role `viewer` · read

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | required | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `query` | `str` | `''` | Text to match in turns: lowercased tokens of 2+ characters, stop words dropped, at most 32 kept; empty reads by time window or thread alone. |
| `since` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | Inclusive lower bound on the turn's observed time; `None` = unbounded. |
| `until` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | Inclusive upper bound on the turn's observed time; `None` = unbounded. |
| `thread` | `str` | `''` | Restrict to one conversation (the session_id the turns were ingested under). |
| `role` | `Literal['', 'user', 'assistant']` | `''` | Only turns of this speaker role; empty returns turns of every role. |
| `match` | `Literal['all', 'any']` | `'all'` | `all`: a turn must carry every query token; `any`: at least one of them. |
| `order` | `Literal['auto', 'recent', 'relevance']` | `'auto'` | `recent` = newest first, `relevance` = most matched tokens first, `auto` = relevance with a query, else recent. |
| `top_k` | `int` | `20` | At most this many turns per page. |
| `cursor` | `str` | `''` | `next_cursor` of the previous page in newest-first order; empty starts at the top. |
| `offset` | `int` | `0` | Turns to skip in relevance order; pass the previous page's `next_offset`. |
| `max_chars` | `int` | `600` | Per-turn content cap; a long turn is cut and flagged `truncated`. |
| `read_scope` | `Literal['namespace', 'own_user', 'own_session']` | `'namespace'` | Same semantics as memory.search.read_scope. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `turns` | `list[_RecallTurn]` | The matching turns of this page, each with content cut to `max_chars`. |
| `total_matched` | `int` | Turns matching the filter in the whole namespace scope, not just this page: "showing 20 of 124". |
| `returned` | `int` | Number of turns in this page. |
| `has_more` | `bool` | True when another page exists after this one. |
| `next_cursor` | `str` | Newest-first paging token; empty when exhausted or in relevance order. |
| `next_offset` | `int` | Relevance paging offset; -1 when exhausted or in newest-first order. |
| `order` | `Literal['recent', 'relevance']` | The order actually used, after `auto` is resolved. |
| `query_tokens` | `list[str]` | The tokens the query was reduced to and matched on. |
| `tokens_returned` | `int` | Estimated prompt tokens of the returned content (chars / 4). |
