## `memory.record.query`

Typed records of one schema by field filters and predicates, as of a time.

`POST /v1/memory.record.query` · MCP `loom_memory_record_query` · role `viewer` · read

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `schema_name` | `str` | required | The schema whose active records are read. |
| `filters` | `dict[str, str]` | *(computed)* | Field name → exact string value (state `value`); all must match. |
| `predicates` | `list[RecordPredicate]` | *(computed)* | Typed comparisons or state checks, AND-composed with `filters`. |
| `as_of` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | Only records whose `valid_at`..`valid_to` interval covers this instant; None = no bound. |
| `limit` | `int` | `100` | At most this many records (1–1000), most recently updated first. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` | `list[MemoryRecordRow]` | Matching active records, most recently updated first. |
| `truncated` | `bool` | True when more records matched than `limit`. |

## `memory.record.write`

Write one typed record (schema name + fields, optional validity window); a newer record for the same key supersedes the old.

`POST /v1/memory.record.write` · MCP `loom_memory_record_write` · role `writer` · write · audited

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `schema_name` | `str` | required | An `active` schema of the namespace, else 404 SCHEMA_NOT_FOUND. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | `''` | The logical key; empty derives it from identity fields, or leaves the record anonymous. |
| `memory_id` | `str \| None` | `None` | The memory row this record cites; stored on the record and on its conflict rows. |
| `agent` | `str` | `''` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `fields` | `dict[str, RecordFieldInput]` | required | Field name → value and state; names outside the schema or missing required ones are 400. |
| `valid_at` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | When the fact became true in the world; closes the superseded record's `valid_to`. |
| `valid_to` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | When the fact stops being true; None = open-ended. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `record_id` | `str` | The new record's id; every write mints a fresh one. |
| `field_count` | `int` | Typed field rows written, including fields kept from the superseded record. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | The logical key the record landed on: the caller's, or one derived from the schema's identity fields, or "" (anonymous — no supersession). |
| `key_source` | `Literal['caller', 'identity', 'anonymous']` | Where `memory_key` came from: the caller, the identity fields, or none. |
| `fold` | `dict[str, Any]` | Supersession is a field-level fold, not a whole-record replace: {agreed, filled_from_prior, added, unioned, changed:[{field, prior, incoming}]} against the record this write superseded; empty when there was none. |
| `superseded_record_id` | `str` | The key's previously active record, now `superseded`; empty when there was none. |
| `conflicts` | `int` | Field disagreements with the superseded record written to the conflicts table. |

## `memory.redact`

Scrub the value of a historical memory row, preserving its audit entry.

`POST /v1/memory.redact` · MCP `loom_memory_redact` · role `admin` · idempotent · audited · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `memory_id` | `str` | required | The id every version of the memory shares; `version` picks the historical row. |
| `version` | `int` | required | target row's version (from memory.set / memory.history) |
| `reason` | `str` | `''` | short justification recorded in the audit log |
| `redacted_by` | `str` | `''` | actor for the audit row (caller-supplied) |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `redacted` | `bool` | False when memory_id or that version is not found, or the caller is not admin of its namespace. |
| `refused_head` | `bool` | True when the target was the live head |
| `redacted_at` | `datetime \| None` | UTC time of the scrub; None when nothing was redacted. |
| `cache_rows_deleted` | `int` | The cached answers whose window held the redacted key or a profile key the redact reached, deleted with it: the stored text that quoted the value. |
| `precedent_rows_deleted` | `int` | Stored `memory.ask` precedents that quoted the redacted key or a profile key the redact reached, deleted with it, across the org for a profile key. |

## `memory.reindex`

Re-embed a namespace's memories whose vectors were made by another embedding model (or all of them with `force`).

`POST /v1/memory.reindex` · MCP `loom_memory_reindex` · role `admin` · idempotent · audited · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `limit` | `int` | `200` | Max rows per call (bounded to avoid spiking the embedder / holding CH locks). |
| `force` | `bool` | `False` | Also re-embed rows already matching the current model (force a clean rebuild). |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `processed` | `int` | Rows re-embedded in this call; call again until it is below `limit`. |
| `skipped_already_current` | `int` | Always 0: rows already on the current model are not read unless `force`. |
| `target_model` | `str` | The embedding model the rows were re-embedded under (the current one). |
| `target_dim` | `int` | The vector dimension of that model. |

## `memory.reject`

Mark a memory as explicitly rejected (extractor / user review decided the candidate fact is wrong), so it isn't re-extracted.

`POST /v1/memory.reject` · MCP `loom_memory_reject` · role `writer` · idempotent · audited · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | required | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | required | The memory to mark `rejected`, matched on org, namespace, agent, user and key. |
| `rejection_reason` | `str` | `''` | Stored as the row's `rejection_reason`; empty stores none. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rejected` | `bool` | Always True: the status update is issued whether or not a row matched. |
| `rejected_at` | `datetime \| None` | The server time the update was issued. |

## `memory.related`

Find memories sharing entities with the source memory.

`POST /v1/memory.related` · MCP `loom_memory_related` · role `viewer` · read

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | required | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | required | The source memory, looked up under the caller's full identity tuple. |
| `top_k` | `int` | `10` | At most this many related memories (1–100), most shared entities first. |
| `min_overlap` | `int` | `1` | Min overlapping entities to qualify. 1 = any shared entity. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `results` | `list[_MemoryRelatedHit]` | Live memories sharing entities with the source (the source excluded), by overlap. |
| `source_entities` | `list[str]` | The entities on the source row; empty when it is missing or has none. |
| `reason` | `str` | Reason code when results=[] for a precondition (not an empty result set): "source_not_found" \| "source_has_no_entities". |

## `memory.resolve_orphan_duplicates`

Scan (org, namespace) for orphaned duplicate rows and re-activate them.

`POST /v1/memory.resolve_orphan_duplicates` · MCP `loom_memory_resolve_orphan_duplicates` · role `writer` · idempotent · audited

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `limit` | `int` | `500` | Max orphan rows to re-activate per call. |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | `False` | True lists the orphan candidates without re-activating them. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `candidates` | `int` | Orphan duplicates the scan matched. |
| `reactivated` | `int` | Rows re-emitted status='active' (0 under dry_run). |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | Echo of the request's `dry_run`. |
| `memory_ids` | `list[str]` | memory_ids of the affected (candidate) rows. |

## `memory.restore`

Bring back a deleted memory (within 14 days) or one Loom retired on its own.

`POST /v1/memory.restore` · MCP `loom_memory_restore` · role `writer` · idempotent · audited

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | required | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | required | The key to restore, under this exact identity (no namespace-wide fallback). |
| `if_superseded_by` | `str` | `''` | Precondition: restore only a row still retired behind this memory, as a `memory.auto_supersede` record names it; a row deleted, revived or retired behind another memory since is left as it is. |
| `only_if_superseded` | `bool` | `False` | Precondition: restore only a row still retired (`superseded`), never undo a delete. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `restored` | `bool` | True when a live version was written back; False on a no-op, a miss or `expired`. |
| `memory_id` | `str \| None` | Empty / None when nothing was tombstoned or superseded for this key (no-op). |
| `version` | `int \| None` | Version of the restored row, or of the already-live row on a no-op. |
| `expired` | `bool` | Surfaces "you missed the window" cleanly rather than 404-ing. |
| `from_status` | `str` | What the row was restored FROM: "tombstoned" (a delete undone) or "superseded" (an automatic retirement reversed). |

## `memory.search`

Semantic search over the agent's own memory.

`POST /v1/memory.search` · MCP `loom_memory_search` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'*'` | Defaults to "*" = read ALL agents in the accessible namespaces: membership is the read boundary, agent is authorship metadata. |
| `render` | `Literal['', 'reader']` | `''` | render="reader": also return `reader_block` + `reader_instructions`, the hits rendered and instructed the way memory.ask reads them. |
| `query` | `str` | required | The natural-language question or keywords to search for; it is embedded for the semantic legs and tokenized for the lexical ones. |
| `memory_type` | `Literal['semantic', 'procedural', 'preference', 'reflection', 'decision'] \| None` | `None` | None = every searchable type except the hidden-by-default ones (reflection). "reflection" = only process lessons (what worked / failed in past runs), which never surface in an unfiltered search. |
| `tags` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | OR-filter on tags (set semantics). |
| `scope` | `Literal['private', 'shared']` | `'private'` | Which rows to read: "private" = per-agent rows (narrowed to `agent` when it names one), "shared" = rows promoted to the namespace's shared scope. |
| `namespace_scope` | `Literal['this', 'all_mine'] \| None` | `None` | "this" reads input.namespace only; "all_mine" also the caller's own namespaces, see docs/concepts/identities-and-namespaces.md#reading-several-namespaces. |
| `search_mode` | `Literal['semantic', 'lexical', 'hybrid', 'bm25_hybrid', 'related', 'graph', 'rrf', 'temporal']` | `'rrf'` | Recall fusion mode. |
| `recipe` | `Literal['', 'fast', 'balanced', 'quality', 'verbatim', 'code', 'temporal', 'graph']` | `''` | Named presets over the lower-level knobs. |
| `alpha` | `float` | `0.5` | Lexical weight for `search_mode` "hybrid" / "bm25_hybrid": the score is alpha * lexical + (1 - alpha) * cosine. |
| `include_top_n_unmatched` | `int` | `0` | When > 0 and a reranker is configured, fetch this many extra candidates by recency to widen the reranker's pool. |
| `include_tags` | `bool` | `False` | Carry each hit's `tags` on the response. |
| `include_usage` | `bool` | `False` | Carry each hit's reliance counters on the response — `reinforcement_count` (the folded rank signal), `used_count` (an agent's label: memory.outcome used / run.complete memories_used), `used_cited_count` (memory.ask's own credit for citing… |
| `include_duplicates` | `bool` | `False` | A `status='duplicate'` row (set-time dedup at 0.97 cosine named its canonical in `duplicate_of`) is not served; its canonical takes the slot, disclosed on the hit as `resolved_from`. |
| `include_superseded` | `bool` | `False` | A `status='superseded'` row (a later write replaced it) is not served unless asked. |
| `include_proposed` | `bool` | `False` | `status='proposed'` rows (facts written for trial, accepted or rejected on graded run outcomes) are served only here, when asked. |
| `explain` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Carry per-hit `explanation` and `score_components`. |
| `legs` | `list[Literal['memory', 'sessions']] \| None` | `None` | The legs the caller can show. |
| `auto_touch` | `bool` | `True` | Record append-only recall usage for every returned row (powers recall_count / last_recalled_at via loom.memory_usage_*, no read-path mutation of loom.memory). |
| `user_id` | `str \| None` | `None` | filter by user_id (for preference recall) |
| `run_id` | `str \| None` | `None` | only rows written under this run; unset or "-" reads every run |
| `session_id` | `str \| None` | `None` | Filter by session_id. |
| `session_ids` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Restrict to a set of sessions: a caller may pin its own. |
| `exclude_keys` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Keys the caller already holds and does not want served again: dropped from the ranked pool BEFORE the window is assembled, so the window fills from the next-best candidates instead of returning a shorter list. |
| `quality_filter` | `bool` | `False` | Drop stored rows that are not facts (trajectory steps, session narration, tool tips, code-location trivia, probes, one-moment status — server/memory/domain/fact_quality.py) and restatements of a higher-ranked fact from the pool before the… |
| `read_scope` | `Literal['namespace', 'own_user', 'own_session']` | `'namespace'` | How far this read may reach inside each namespace: "namespace" — every row the token can access (membership is the read boundary; the default). "own_user" — only rows written under `user_id`, which must be set. "own_session" — only rows… |
| `entity_filter` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | If non-empty, OR-match against extracted entities — rows whose `entities` array intersects this list are boosted alongside cosine matches. |
| `category` | `str` | `''` | If set, restrict the search to memories assigned to this category (via namespace.register_category + memory.assign_category). |
| `tags_soft` | `bool` | `False` | --- Soft metadata ranking (sharpen recall without the coverage loss of a hard filter). |
| `tag_boost` | `float` | `0.3` | Max rank contribution from tag overlap when tags_soft (scaled by fraction of query tags present). |
| `category_soft` | `bool` | `False` | True turns `category` from a hard filter into a rank boost of `category_boost` for its members; False (default) returns members only. |
| `category_boost` | `float` | `0.3` | Rank contribution for category members when category_soft. |
| `confidence_weight` | `float` | `0.1` | Per-request weight on stored `confidence` in the blended rank score. |
| `prior_cap` | `float \| None` | `None` | Cap on the discretionary-prior group (confidence + soft tag/category) so it tiebreaks rather than re-ranks. |
| `sensitivity_penalty` | `float \| None` | `None` | Demotion applied to rows tagged `sensitivity:medium\|high`. |
| `rrf_adaptive_lexical` | `bool \| None` | `None` | RRF only: down-weight the lexical leg for code/path-shaped queries. |
| `demote_tags` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Hard-demote: rows whose `tags` intersect this list are pushed to the bottom of the ranking (large negative term) but NOT dropped — for known-noise markers (e.g. "recurring_false_positive") that still surface. |
| `reinforcement_weight` | `float \| None` | `None` | Decayed-reinforcement boost overrides (None → server default). weight sizes the boost from reinforcement_count (recall + positive memory.outcome), half_life_days sets how fast it decays since last reinforcement. |
| `recency_pool_weight` | `float \| None` | `None` | Per-request override of the recency pool re-rank weight applied on a recency-intent query; None = the namespace's retrieval_defaults, else the deployment default (0.0 = off). |
| `reinforcement_half_life_days` | `float \| None` | `None` | Days for the reinforcement boost to halve since a row was last reinforced; None = the deployment default. |
| `mention_boost` | `float \| None` | `None` | Pool-consensus mention boost: hits whose entities the rest of the candidate pool also mentions move up by at most prior_cap. |
| `ground_relative_dates` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Append the row's resolved date to a fact excerpt that still carries a bare relative phrase ("… yesterday (on 2023-11-16)"). |
| `reinforcement_half_life_use_scale` | `float \| None` | `None` | Use-scaled half-life: half_life · (1 + scale · log1p(reinforcement_count − 1)). |
| `key_match` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Key-match arm override: None → deployment default (LOOM_MEMORY_SEARCH_KEY_MATCH_MODE); True/False forces it for this request. |
| `key_match_mode` | `Literal['always', 'gated', 'off'] \| None` | `None` | `always` \| `gated` \| `off` for this request; None → the deployment default (LOOM_MEMORY_SEARCH_KEY_MATCH_MODE). |
| `digest_descent` | `bool \| None` | `None` | When a session digest ranks in the top-m of the pool, pull that session's own top-k facts in as candidates. |
| `role` | `str` | `''` | The calling agent's role in a multi-agent run — planner, executor, critic, or the team's own word. |
| `top_k` | `int` | `5` | At most this many hits to return (capped at 500, and lower by a per-token ceiling reported in `top_k_ceiling`). |
| `key_axis` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Key-embedding axis. |
| `bodies` | `Literal['full', 'excerpt', 'none', 'unit', 'source']` | `'full'` | What each hit carries back. |
| `body_budget_tokens` | `int` | `4000` | Cap 32,000: a run trace is ~4,000 tokens whole, and a constraint that cites three earlier steps needs three whole traces plus the base; a 12,000 cap clips the third to 1,200 chars without its result. |
| `source_span_chars` | `int` | `0` | bodies="source": 0 serves the whole linked passage; N serves an N-character window centred on the span the fact was extracted from (memory_belief_sources.char_start/char_end): an evidence capsule at a fraction of the trace-sized window. |
| `paging` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Paging. |
| `page` | `str` | `''` | A `next_page` handle from an earlier call; serves that list's next slice with no retrieval. |
| `recent_first` | `int` | `0` | Run-scoped recency tier. |
| `anchor_first` | `int` | `0` | Run-scoped anchor tier: the N OLDEST memories of this identity — restricted to `run_id` when the request carries one — are placed first, ahead of similarity hits, within top_k. |
| `per_speaker_quota` | `int \| None` | `None` | Per-speaker quota: each speaker in the fused pool is guaranteed up to this many rows of the top_k before the remainder fills by rank, so one voice of a two-party conversation cannot take the whole window. |
| `min_body_chars` | `int` | `0` | Drop hits whose body is shorter than this many characters (0 = off). |
| `graph_seed` | `Literal['', 'query', 'recent', 'both']` | `''` | Where the graph walk starts: "query" = the question's entities and nearest triples (the default); "recent" = the entities of this identity's newest memories (the session's when session_id is set), so what was just talked about reaches the… |
| `diversify` | `Literal['', 'none', 'session']` | `''` | Evidence completion. "session": at most `diversify_session_cap` hits per source session in the block; the rest of a session's rows yield their slot to the next session in rank order. |
| `diversify_session_cap` | `int \| None` | `None` | Per-session cap for diversify="session"; None = max(2, top_k // 3). |
| `summary_cap` | `int \| None` | `None` | At most this many digest rows (source summary / entity_summary) in the final block; None or 0 = unbounded. |
| `chunk_cap_share` | `float \| None` | `None` | Fact rows first: the largest share of the block that verbatim chunk rows may hold; surplus slots go to the best unreached fact rows. |
| `floor_mode` | `Literal['readmit', 'ids_only', 'drop'] \| None` | `None` | What happens to hits under the similarity floor when top_k is set. |
| `min_similarity` | `float \| None` | `None` | The similarity below which a hit is noise for THIS read. |
| `chunk_max_share` | `float \| None` | `None` | At most this share of the window is verbatim chunks (the chunk cap, per read). |
| `personalization` | `Literal['full', 'none']` | `'full'` | Personalization arm. "full" = the default ranking. "none" drops every user-derived rank term in every mode — preference boost, discretionary prior group, reinforcement — and keeps relevance terms. |
| `observation_date` | `str` | `''` | ISO YYYY-MM-DD anchor for resolving relative time in the query; when set the resolved date is appended to the embedded query text. |
| `rerank` | `str` | `''` | Per-request reranker override. |
| `retrieval_budget` | `Literal['fast', 'standard', 'deep']` | `'standard'` | Cost posture. "standard" stages cheap recall first, spending expensive LLM/graph/rerank legs only when the planner or fallback gates justify them. "fast" makes no LLM call (as recipe "fast"); "deep" allows upfront expensive recall. |
| `hyde` | `bool` | `True` | HyDE: embed an LLM-generated hypothetical answer instead of the raw query to close the question/stored-phrasing vocabulary gap. |
| `as_of` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | As-of replay filter (coalesce(valid_at, created_at) <= as_of), denormalized onto memory_embeddings so vector_search applies it without joining loom.memory. |
| `as_of_basis` | `Literal['valid_time', 'knowledge_time']` | `'valid_time'` | Which time axis `as_of` replays: "valid_time" (default; what was true as of then) or "knowledge_time" (what loom had learned by then — created_at only, ignoring valid_at; the incremental-ingest knowledge cutoff). |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `results` | `list[_MemorySearchHit]` | The ranked hits, best first; empty when nothing passed the noise floor. |
| `reader_block` | `str` | render="reader" only: the results as one prompt block ("[date] [key] (type) excerpt", ordered as memory.ask would read them) and the synthesizer's instructions, so an external reader scores what the ask reader scores on the same hits. |
| `reader_instructions` | `str` | render="reader" only: the synthesizer instructions memory.ask pairs with `reader_block`; empty otherwise. |
| `bodies_returned` | `int` | bodies="unit" accounting: whole values served / withheld for budget, and the estimated tokens those bodies added (len/4). |
| `bodies_elided` | `int` | Hits whose whole value was withheld because `body_budget_tokens` ran out. |
| `tokens_returned` | `int` | Estimated tokens (chars / 4) the whole values served under bodies="unit" added. |
| `namespaces_searched` | `list[str]` | The namespaces in this search's scope: the addressed one first, then the fan-out under namespace_scope=all_mine. |
| `namespaces_skipped` | `list[str]` | Namespaces of the caller the fan-out did not read because it stops at `memory_search_fanout_max_namespaces`; address one by name to search it. |
| `candidates_total` | `int` | Distinct memories in the fused pool before the top_k cut ("showing 10 of 124"); the handle that serves the next slice when the caller asked for paging and there was more; and this page's offset into the parked list (0 for a fresh search). |
| `next_page` | `str` | Handle to pass as `page` for the next slice; empty when `paging` was off or no more candidates remained. |
| `page_offset` | `int` | This page's offset into the parked list; 0 for a fresh search. |
| `chunk_share` | `float` | Share of the returned window that is verbatim chunks: the reader for "did chunks crowd out the facts" on the ledger. |
| `embedding_model` | `str` | The embedding model the query was embedded with. |
| `next` | `str` | Protocol nudge, set only when the call carried a run_id: how to report which of these hits the agent relied on (run.complete memories_used). |
| `scratchpad` | `str` | The identity's working-memory blocks, rendered as markdown, when the call named a session_id or run_id and a block exists for that scope. |
| `scratchpad_blocks` | `int` | How many working-memory blocks `scratchpad` rendered; 0 = none. |
| `reinforcement` | `str \| None` | Whether this read's recall credit was written. |
| `graph_seeds` | `int` | Graph-mode diagnostics, summed across the cross-namespace fan-out. graph_seeds = 1-hop seed entities; graph_neighbors_added = neighbors materialized from entity_edges and fed to rank fusion as graph_overlap. |
| `graph_neighbors_added` | `int` | Neighbor memories pulled in from entity edges and fused as graph overlap; 0 when graph expansion did not run or found none. |
| `triples_extracted_from_query` | `int` | Relation-typing diagnostics: (s,v,o) triples pulled from the query, and the deduped count of memory_keys with matching stored triples. |
| `triples_matched` | `int` | Distinct memories whose stored triples matched a query triple. |
| `set_expansion_phrases` | `int` | How many instance phrases the set-question expansion ran as extra legs (0 = trigger did not fire or the lever is off). |
| `top_k_ceiling` | `int` | Abstention signal: True when retrieval can't honestly answer — results empty after the noise floor, or top similarity below LOOM_MEMORY_SEARCH_ABSTAIN_THRESHOLD. |
| `abstain` | `bool` | True when retrieval cannot honestly answer: no hit survived the noise floor, the top similarity or calibrated confidence was too low, or a named entity is absent. |
| `abstain_reason` | `str` | Human-readable reason for `abstain`; empty when it is False. |
| `abstain_code` | `Literal['', 'no_match', 'below_threshold', 'low_calibrated_confidence', 'entity_absent', 'page_expired']` | Bounded machine-readable companion to `abstain_reason`. |
| `degraded` | `list[str]` | Providers that fell back on this read and what the response did instead (`rerank: input_order_kept (ReadTimeout)`). |
| `recipe` | `str` | Named recipe applied (if any) + a terse final scoring posture. |
| `score_explanation` | `str` | Terse scoring posture: mode, recipe, hyde, rerank and tag filter, then the retrieval plan (`mode=rrf, hyde=on; plan=...`). |
| `retrieval_confidence` | `float` | Calibrated confidence in the hit set, 0 to 1, from top similarity, top-two margin, route agreement and result count; 0 on no hits. |
| `retrieval_risk` | `Literal['low', 'medium', 'high', 'abstain']` | Risk label from `retrieval_confidence`: "low" (>= 0.75), "medium" (>= 0.55), "high" (below), "abstain" (below the abstain thresholds). |
| `route_agreement` | `float` | Share of the retrieval routes that ran (semantic, graph, triples, evidence, extra legs) that also found support, 0 to 1. |
| `calibration_explanation` | `str` | The inputs behind `retrieval_confidence`: top_similarity, margin, route_agreement, evidence_support (and constrained=true when set). |
| `fallback_rounds_used` | `int` | Recursive-fallback cascade accounting (iterative-judge). rounds_used = rounds spent (capped at LOOM_MEMORY_SEARCH_FALLBACK_MAX_ROUNDS); budget_exhausted = a leg was denied by the round/wall-clock cap; elapsed_ms = wall-clock in the cascade. |
| `fallback_budget_exhausted` | `bool` | True when a fallback leg was denied by the round or wall-clock cap. |
| `fallback_elapsed_ms` | `int` | Wall-clock milliseconds spent in the fallback cascade. |
| `retrieval_plan` | `str` | Planner diagnostics: pre-execution shape estimate + best-effort actual work. |
| `retrieval_cost_estimate` | `dict[str, Any]` | Pre-execution work estimate: budget_class, llm_calls, embedding_calls, vector / lexical / graph / structured queries, candidate_pool, top_k. |
| `retrieval_work` | `dict[str, Any]` | Work actually done: per-stage counters (e.g. |
| `pending_extraction` | `int` | Deferred set_from_messages batches not yet extracted in the searched scope. >0 means "a save is in flight", so an empty or thin result is not evidence of absence; re-ask after the worker runs. |
| `derived_aggregate` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | Exact in-ClickHouse aggregate for derived-answer queries (aggregational / temporal_diff) over per-occurrence rows — what the vector planes structurally can't produce. |

## `memory.search_trace`

Same shape as memory.search; returns the vector leg's per-candidate scoring breakdown (no fusion, assembly or reranker).

`POST /v1/memory.search_trace` · MCP `loom_memory_search_trace` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'*'` | Defaults to "*" = read ALL agents in the accessible namespaces: membership is the read boundary, agent is authorship metadata. |
| `render` | `Literal['', 'reader']` | `''` | render="reader": also return `reader_block` + `reader_instructions`, the hits rendered and instructed the way memory.ask reads them. |
| `query` | `str` | required | The natural-language question or keywords to search for; it is embedded for the semantic legs and tokenized for the lexical ones. |
| `memory_type` | `Literal['semantic', 'procedural', 'preference', 'reflection', 'decision'] \| None` | `None` | None = every searchable type except the hidden-by-default ones (reflection). "reflection" = only process lessons (what worked / failed in past runs), which never surface in an unfiltered search. |
| `tags` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | OR-filter on tags (set semantics). |
| `scope` | `Literal['private', 'shared']` | `'private'` | Which rows to read: "private" = per-agent rows (narrowed to `agent` when it names one), "shared" = rows promoted to the namespace's shared scope. |
| `namespace_scope` | `Literal['this', 'all_mine'] \| None` | `None` | "this" reads input.namespace only; "all_mine" also the caller's own namespaces, see docs/concepts/identities-and-namespaces.md#reading-several-namespaces. |
| `search_mode` | `Literal['semantic', 'lexical', 'hybrid', 'bm25_hybrid', 'related', 'graph', 'rrf', 'temporal']` | `'rrf'` | Recall fusion mode. |
| `recipe` | `Literal['', 'fast', 'balanced', 'quality', 'verbatim', 'code', 'temporal', 'graph']` | `''` | Named presets over the lower-level knobs. |
| `alpha` | `float` | `0.5` | Lexical weight for `search_mode` "hybrid" / "bm25_hybrid": the score is alpha * lexical + (1 - alpha) * cosine. |
| `include_top_n_unmatched` | `int` | `0` | When > 0 and a reranker is configured, fetch this many extra candidates by recency to widen the reranker's pool. |
| `include_tags` | `bool` | `False` | Carry each hit's `tags` on the response. |
| `include_usage` | `bool` | `False` | Carry each hit's reliance counters on the response — `reinforcement_count` (the folded rank signal), `used_count` (an agent's label: memory.outcome used / run.complete memories_used), `used_cited_count` (memory.ask's own credit for citing… |
| `include_duplicates` | `bool` | `False` | A `status='duplicate'` row (set-time dedup at 0.97 cosine named its canonical in `duplicate_of`) is not served; its canonical takes the slot, disclosed on the hit as `resolved_from`. |
| `include_superseded` | `bool` | `False` | A `status='superseded'` row (a later write replaced it) is not served unless asked. |
| `include_proposed` | `bool` | `False` | `status='proposed'` rows (facts written for trial, accepted or rejected on graded run outcomes) are served only here, when asked. |
| `explain` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Carry per-hit `explanation` and `score_components`. |
| `legs` | `list[Literal['memory', 'sessions']] \| None` | `None` | The legs the caller can show. |
| `auto_touch` | `bool` | `True` | Record append-only recall usage for every returned row (powers recall_count / last_recalled_at via loom.memory_usage_*, no read-path mutation of loom.memory). |
| `user_id` | `str \| None` | `None` | filter by user_id (for preference recall) |
| `run_id` | `str \| None` | `None` | only rows written under this run; unset or "-" reads every run |
| `session_id` | `str \| None` | `None` | Filter by session_id. |
| `session_ids` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Restrict to a set of sessions: a caller may pin its own. |
| `exclude_keys` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Keys the caller already holds and does not want served again: dropped from the ranked pool BEFORE the window is assembled, so the window fills from the next-best candidates instead of returning a shorter list. |
| `quality_filter` | `bool` | `False` | Drop stored rows that are not facts (trajectory steps, session narration, tool tips, code-location trivia, probes, one-moment status — server/memory/domain/fact_quality.py) and restatements of a higher-ranked fact from the pool before the… |
| `read_scope` | `Literal['namespace', 'own_user', 'own_session']` | `'namespace'` | How far this read may reach inside each namespace: "namespace" — every row the token can access (membership is the read boundary; the default). "own_user" — only rows written under `user_id`, which must be set. "own_session" — only rows… |
| `entity_filter` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | If non-empty, OR-match against extracted entities — rows whose `entities` array intersects this list are boosted alongside cosine matches. |
| `category` | `str` | `''` | If set, restrict the search to memories assigned to this category (via namespace.register_category + memory.assign_category). |
| `tags_soft` | `bool` | `False` | --- Soft metadata ranking (sharpen recall without the coverage loss of a hard filter). |
| `tag_boost` | `float` | `0.3` | Max rank contribution from tag overlap when tags_soft (scaled by fraction of query tags present). |
| `category_soft` | `bool` | `False` | True turns `category` from a hard filter into a rank boost of `category_boost` for its members; False (default) returns members only. |
| `category_boost` | `float` | `0.3` | Rank contribution for category members when category_soft. |
| `confidence_weight` | `float` | `0.1` | Per-request weight on stored `confidence` in the blended rank score. |
| `prior_cap` | `float \| None` | `None` | Cap on the discretionary-prior group (confidence + soft tag/category) so it tiebreaks rather than re-ranks. |
| `sensitivity_penalty` | `float \| None` | `None` | Demotion applied to rows tagged `sensitivity:medium\|high`. |
| `rrf_adaptive_lexical` | `bool \| None` | `None` | RRF only: down-weight the lexical leg for code/path-shaped queries. |
| `demote_tags` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Hard-demote: rows whose `tags` intersect this list are pushed to the bottom of the ranking (large negative term) but NOT dropped — for known-noise markers (e.g. "recurring_false_positive") that still surface. |
| `reinforcement_weight` | `float \| None` | `None` | Decayed-reinforcement boost overrides (None → server default). weight sizes the boost from reinforcement_count (recall + positive memory.outcome), half_life_days sets how fast it decays since last reinforcement. |
| `recency_pool_weight` | `float \| None` | `None` | Per-request override of the recency pool re-rank weight applied on a recency-intent query; None = the namespace's retrieval_defaults, else the deployment default (0.0 = off). |
| `reinforcement_half_life_days` | `float \| None` | `None` | Days for the reinforcement boost to halve since a row was last reinforced; None = the deployment default. |
| `mention_boost` | `float \| None` | `None` | Pool-consensus mention boost: hits whose entities the rest of the candidate pool also mentions move up by at most prior_cap. |
| `ground_relative_dates` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Append the row's resolved date to a fact excerpt that still carries a bare relative phrase ("… yesterday (on 2023-11-16)"). |
| `reinforcement_half_life_use_scale` | `float \| None` | `None` | Use-scaled half-life: half_life · (1 + scale · log1p(reinforcement_count − 1)). |
| `key_match` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Key-match arm override: None → deployment default (LOOM_MEMORY_SEARCH_KEY_MATCH_MODE); True/False forces it for this request. |
| `key_match_mode` | `Literal['always', 'gated', 'off'] \| None` | `None` | `always` \| `gated` \| `off` for this request; None → the deployment default (LOOM_MEMORY_SEARCH_KEY_MATCH_MODE). |
| `digest_descent` | `bool \| None` | `None` | When a session digest ranks in the top-m of the pool, pull that session's own top-k facts in as candidates. |
| `role` | `str` | `''` | The calling agent's role in a multi-agent run — planner, executor, critic, or the team's own word. |
| `top_k` | `int` | `5` | At most this many hits to return (capped at 500, and lower by a per-token ceiling reported in `top_k_ceiling`). |
| `key_axis` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Key-embedding axis. |
| `bodies` | `Literal['full', 'excerpt', 'none', 'unit', 'source']` | `'full'` | What each hit carries back. |
| `body_budget_tokens` | `int` | `4000` | Cap 32,000: a run trace is ~4,000 tokens whole, and a constraint that cites three earlier steps needs three whole traces plus the base; a 12,000 cap clips the third to 1,200 chars without its result. |
| `source_span_chars` | `int` | `0` | bodies="source": 0 serves the whole linked passage; N serves an N-character window centred on the span the fact was extracted from (memory_belief_sources.char_start/char_end): an evidence capsule at a fraction of the trace-sized window. |
| `paging` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Paging. |
| `page` | `str` | `''` | A `next_page` handle from an earlier call; serves that list's next slice with no retrieval. |
| `recent_first` | `int` | `0` | Run-scoped recency tier. |
| `anchor_first` | `int` | `0` | Run-scoped anchor tier: the N OLDEST memories of this identity — restricted to `run_id` when the request carries one — are placed first, ahead of similarity hits, within top_k. |
| `per_speaker_quota` | `int \| None` | `None` | Per-speaker quota: each speaker in the fused pool is guaranteed up to this many rows of the top_k before the remainder fills by rank, so one voice of a two-party conversation cannot take the whole window. |
| `min_body_chars` | `int` | `0` | Drop hits whose body is shorter than this many characters (0 = off). |
| `graph_seed` | `Literal['', 'query', 'recent', 'both']` | `''` | Where the graph walk starts: "query" = the question's entities and nearest triples (the default); "recent" = the entities of this identity's newest memories (the session's when session_id is set), so what was just talked about reaches the… |
| `diversify` | `Literal['', 'none', 'session']` | `''` | Evidence completion. "session": at most `diversify_session_cap` hits per source session in the block; the rest of a session's rows yield their slot to the next session in rank order. |
| `diversify_session_cap` | `int \| None` | `None` | Per-session cap for diversify="session"; None = max(2, top_k // 3). |
| `summary_cap` | `int \| None` | `None` | At most this many digest rows (source summary / entity_summary) in the final block; None or 0 = unbounded. |
| `chunk_cap_share` | `float \| None` | `None` | Fact rows first: the largest share of the block that verbatim chunk rows may hold; surplus slots go to the best unreached fact rows. |
| `floor_mode` | `Literal['readmit', 'ids_only', 'drop'] \| None` | `None` | What happens to hits under the similarity floor when top_k is set. |
| `min_similarity` | `float \| None` | `None` | The similarity below which a hit is noise for THIS read. |
| `chunk_max_share` | `float \| None` | `None` | At most this share of the window is verbatim chunks (the chunk cap, per read). |
| `personalization` | `Literal['full', 'none']` | `'full'` | Personalization arm. "full" = the default ranking. "none" drops every user-derived rank term in every mode — preference boost, discretionary prior group, reinforcement — and keeps relevance terms. |
| `observation_date` | `str` | `''` | ISO YYYY-MM-DD anchor for resolving relative time in the query; when set the resolved date is appended to the embedded query text. |
| `rerank` | `str` | `''` | Per-request reranker override. |
| `retrieval_budget` | `Literal['fast', 'standard', 'deep']` | `'standard'` | Cost posture. "standard" stages cheap recall first, spending expensive LLM/graph/rerank legs only when the planner or fallback gates justify them. "fast" makes no LLM call (as recipe "fast"); "deep" allows upfront expensive recall. |
| `hyde` | `bool` | `True` | HyDE: embed an LLM-generated hypothetical answer instead of the raw query to close the question/stored-phrasing vocabulary gap. |
| `as_of` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | As-of replay filter (coalesce(valid_at, created_at) <= as_of), denormalized onto memory_embeddings so vector_search applies it without joining loom.memory. |
| `as_of_basis` | `Literal['valid_time', 'knowledge_time']` | `'valid_time'` | Which time axis `as_of` replays: "valid_time" (default; what was true as of then) or "knowledge_time" (what loom had learned by then — created_at only, ignoring valid_at; the incremental-ingest knowledge cutoff). |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `results` | `list[_SearchTraceHit]` | Every candidate the fact leg scored, in the leg's rank order, with its breakdown. |
| `embedding_model` | `str` | The embedding model the query was embedded with. |
| `entity_filter` | `list[str]` | The request's `entity_filter`, lowercased as it was matched. |
| `query_spellings` | `dict[str, str]` | Query words embedded in the corpus's spelling instead of as typed (`memory_search_query_spelling_max_words`); {} when none was. |
| `query_spellings_skipped` | `bool` | True when the query was embedded as typed because the spelling lookup did not answer (failed, timed out, namespace backing off) or the respelled text's embed failed. |

## `memory.search_trace_log`

Read loom.search_trace_log for a namespace (requires the telemetry flag).

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |

| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |

| `run_id` | `str` | `''` | Only searches made under this run; "" or "-" = every run. |

## `memory.set`

Save a fact to Loom — shared across every AI tool the user runs; native memory is the Claude-only scratchpad.

`POST /v1/memory.set` · MCP `loom_memory_set` · role `writer` · idempotent

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | required | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | required | The key to write; a write to a key that already holds a row adds a new version. |
| `memory_type` | `str` | `'semantic'` | Coarse classification axis (drives procedural memory + tag_registry policy lookups). |
| `value` | `dict[str, Any] \| list[Any] \| str \| int \| float \| bool` | required | The fact itself: plain text, or a JSON object, list or scalar. |
| `tags` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Flexible classification, filterable at recall via MemorySearchInput.tags; per-tag retention/dedup/conflict policy via NamespaceRegisterInput.tag_registry. |
| `entities` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Explicit entities for a point write. |
| `relations` | `list[tuple[str, str, str]]` | *(computed)* | The (subject, relation, object) facts the value states, written to the fact graph and linked to the row as a `memory.bulk_set` entry's are: a single-valued fact closes the older one it replaces and, under `newest_wins`, retires the rows… |
| `files` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | The repo files this memory is about (repo-relative path or bare filename); memory.for_file serves it before an edit of them. |
| `confidence` | `float` | `1.0` | The writer's own confidence in the fact, 0..1 (1.0 = certain). |
| `source_trace` | `str` | `''` | Provenance tag of the write (`conversation:<id>`, `curated_doc://…`); a known prefix decides `source_class` (`conversation:` → extracted), and one starting with `memory.delete_version:` is refused. |
| `source_class` | `str \| None` | `None` | Declare that this content came from outside (a tool result, a page, a document): `external`, or `imported`. |
| `source_resource_id` | `str` | `''` | Provenance pointer to the primary source this fact was cited from — a file path, document id, or URL. |
| `ttl_seconds` | `int \| None` | `None` | Expire the row this many seconds from now. |
| `clear_expiry` | `bool` | `False` | Force expires_at=NULL, ignoring per-type/namespace retention defaults. |
| `on_expire` | `Literal['', 'tombstone', 'demote', 'anonymize']` | `''` | What happens when expires_at passes: '' keeps the row's current action (tombstone for a new row); 'demote' clears the expiry and scales confidence down; 'anonymize' replaces the value with a marker and drops the embeddings, keeping the… |
| `expire_reason` | `str` | `''` | Why the expiry is set (at most 512 chars, not starting with `blacklist.sweep:`); '' keeps the row's current reason. |
| `valid_at` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | Real-world time the fact became true (distinct from created_at and from temporal_anchor). |
| `valid_to` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | Closing bound of the fact's stated validity ("until 2024"); NULL = open interval. |
| `pinned` | `bool` | `False` | True when written via memory.pin (explicit-save) |
| `classify` | `bool` | `False` | Call the namespace's classify_endpoint to derive memory_type from `value`. |
| `if_match_sha256` | `str` | `''` | Optimistic-concurrency precondition: 409 PRECONDITION_FAILED if the live row's SHA-256 doesn't match. |
| `char_limit` | `int \| None` | `None` | Server-enforced char cap on the stringified value (422 on exceed). |
| `sensitivity` | `Literal['', 'low', 'medium', 'high']` | `''` | Sensitivity tier. 'high' = never embedded, searched or in a recency pack; read by key only, audited. '' = detect from the value: credentials, card numbers, SSNs, PINs high; email, phone, IBAN medium. |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | `False` | Run the conflict check and return its verdict, peers and `next` WITHOUT writing — no loom.memory row, no embedding row, no audit hash, no usage event, no supersession. |
| `proposed` | `bool` | `False` | Write the fact as a PROPOSAL (`status='proposed'`): not served by default, served to a read that passes `include_proposed`, and accepted or rejected on the graded outcomes of the runs that used it (`run.grade`, `memory.proposals`… |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `int` | nanosecond version assigned by the server |
| `pinned` | `bool` | True when the stored row is pinned: a `memory.pin`, or a restatement of a pinned row. |
| `memory_id` | `str` | UUID assigned to this insert; usable with memory.get_by_id |
| `content_sha256` | `str` | SHA-256 of the just-written value; usable as if_match_sha256 on next write. |
| `status` | `str` | The written row's lifecycle status (`active`, `duplicate`, `proposed`); "" on a write that stored no row (merge, dry run). |
| `duplicate_of` | `str` | Set when this write was tagged status='duplicate': memory_id of the canonical semantically-identical row. |
| `namespace` | `str` | Echoed so a tool-call response carries citable factual data. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | The key the request named; on a `merge` see `merged_into_key`. |
| `merged_into_key` | `str` | On a `merge` the store already held this content under ANOTHER key; nothing was written at `memory_key`, so a get/lock/update of it finds no row. |
| `degraded` | `list[str]` | Providers that fell back on this write and what the response did instead (`classify: caller_type_kept (ReadTimeout)`). |
| `retyped_from` | `str` | Set when the declared memory_type did not fit the value and the row was stored under another type (currently: 'procedural' on a value that is not a procedure body → 'semantic', tagged retyped_from:procedural). |
| `conflict_verdict` | `str` | What the write-time conflict check decided about THIS write — clear \| merge \| duplicate \| conflict \| refines \| rejected (the last only on a dry run; a real write answers 409). |
| `peers` | `list[MemorySetPeer]` | The rows the verdict was reached against (closest first, at most five): the key is the handle for memory.update, the excerpt what the store holds. |
| `next` | `str` | A short machine hint naming the op to reach for: memory.update(key) on a conflict, memory.pin on a merge the store has seen before, "" otherwise. |
| `noop` | `bool` | True when this call wrote nothing: a `merge` (the store already held the fact; its row was reinforced instead) or a dry run. |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | Echo of the request's dry_run so a tool-call transcript is unambiguous. |
| `advisories` | `list[str]` | One line per thing the server noticed about the VALUE that the agent should fix on its side — currently only "base64-encoded". |
| `chunks_written` | `int` | Verbatim chunk rows this write added to the chunk plane for a long searchable value (0 for a short value, a non-searchable type, a merge or a dry run). |

## `memory.set_from_messages`

Run LLM extraction on `messages` and write the extracted facts.

`POST /v1/memory.set_from_messages` · MCP `loom_memory_set_from_messages` · role `writer` · write

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | required | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `messages` | `list[_Message]` | required | 400, not 100: an unattended session or a grouped batch of sessions is longer than a chat turn, and topic segmentation exists to split exactly that into topic-sized extraction calls. |
| `extra_tags` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Applied to every extracted fact, merged with the LLM-extracted tags. |
| `recalled_keys` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | The memory keys the session's Loom tools SERVED (the plugin's hooks stash them). |
| `session_values` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | The text the session's own Loom tool calls carried — the values they wrote, the queries they asked, the results they got (the plugin reads them from the transcript at SessionEnd). |
| `max_tokens` | `int` | `4096` | Ceiling on the extraction call; default gives headroom for ~40+ facts. |
| `judge_extraction` | `bool` | `False` | Optional second-pass extractor judge (adds an LLM call); off by default. |
| `record_schema` | `dict[str, str \| list[str]] \| None` | `None` | Typed extraction. |
| `memory_key` | `str \| None` | `None` | required iff record_schema is set |
| `observation_date` | `str` | `''` | ISO YYYY-MM-DD anchor for relative time references ("yesterday", "last week"). |
| `llm_cache` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Per-call pin of the extractor's exact-prompt response cache. |
| `detect_updates` | `bool \| None` | `None` | Value-update supersession (memory.app.value_updates): after the write, link each new memory that restates an existing one with a different value token, marking the older side superseded. |
| `last_messages` | `list[_Message]` | *(computed)* | Prior turns from the SAME session not being extracted this call — lets the extractor resolve pronouns/follow-ups/cross-turn references without re-extracting earlier facts. |
| `extraction_instructions` | `str` | `''` | Per-request extraction-prompt suffix for workload-specific tuning. |
| `coverage_sweep` | `bool \| None` | `None` | The coverage sweep (turn- and sentence-level second reading) per call — None = the namespace, then the density gates. |
| `agent_learnings` | `bool \| None` | `None` | None follows memory_extract_agent_learnings (default off); false skips filing the assistant's rules for this call, and true while the setting is off is named in ignored_args. |
| `pipeline_steps` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | *(computed)* | Per-call workflow override. |
| `valid_at` | `datetime \| None` | `None` | Fallback valid_at for facts the extractor didn't anchor itself. |
| `defer` | `bool` | `False` | Capture now, extract later. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `written` | `list[_BulkSetResult]` | Key and version of each extracted fact written; empty on a deferred call. |
| `refused` | `list[_RefusedFact]` | The extracted facts the write refused (a blacklisted, pinned or locked key, or a pinned row close by), with the verdict; not in `written` or the counts. |
| `tokens_in` | `int` | Prompt tokens of the extraction LLM calls. |
| `tokens_out` | `int` | Completion tokens of the extraction LLM calls. |
| `llm_provider` | `str` | The LLM provider that ran the extraction; '' when deferred. |
| `llm_model` | `str` | The model that ran the extraction; '' when deferred. |
| `segments` | `int` | Extraction calls made: 1, or the number of topic segments. |
| `foresight` | `int` | Facts written as time-bounded `foresight` rows. |
| `forgotten` | `int` | Memories retired because the user asked to forget them, and their keys. |
| `forgotten_keys` | `list[str]` | The keys of the memories those forget requests retired. |
| `forget_requests` | `int` | Requests to forget read from the user's own sentences; with `forgotten` it says how many found a row to retire. |
| `about_other` | `int` | Rows written as another person's (`about:other`), whether the extractor said so or the sentence's subject did. |
| `premise_facts` | `int` | The user's facts read from the assistant's premises ("since you enjoy X…"), added to the batch. |
| `learning_candidates` | `int` | Rules the assistant stated about itself that wrote to the learnings queue: a new candidate or this session's support of one (a session restating a rule it already backs counts 0). |
| `ignored_args` | `list[str]` | Request fields the server did not apply: unknown keys, and `agent_learnings=true` while the deployment setting memory_extract_agent_learnings is off. |
| `segmenter` | `str` | Which planner cut them: whole \| size. |
| `cached_tokens_in` | `int` | Subset of tokens_in the provider served from its prompt cache (billed at a discount). |
| `ontology_warnings` | `list[str]` | Extracted entity types / relation verbs outside the namespace's ontology (loom.namespace_ontology). |
| `evidence_ids` | `list[str]` | Evidence-first provenance: set when raw source evidence was persisted before extraction and linked to the written memories. |
| `belief_source_links` | `int` | Links written from the new memories to the stored source evidence rows. |
| `pipeline_errors` | `list[str]` | Fail-open pipeline steps that logged-and-skipped (operator hook unreachable, fetch_existing failed, unknown step id, ...). |
| `value_updates_linked` | `int` | Older memories this ingest marked superseded by a value update (memory.app.value_updates; 0 when detection is off). |
| `stubbed_fields` | `list[str]` | Schema mode only: record_schema fields the extractor could not validate after its retries and wrote as null (never a fabricated value). |
| `degraded` | `list[str]` | Schema mode only: what the response skipped and why, e.g. the memory_records projection for a caller bounded to one user. |
| `deferred` | `bool` | defer=true: nothing extracted yet; `written` is empty and `queue_id` is the handle memory.extraction_status_mine (and memory.extraction_status) report on. |
| `queue_id` | `str` | The queued batch's id for `memory.extraction_status_mine` and `memory.extraction_status`; '' when inline. |
| `deferred_by` | `str` | "" (inline) \| "flag" (the caller passed defer=true) \| "allowlist" (the deployment's extraction_defer_agents chose for the caller) |
| `stage_ms` | `dict[str, float]` | Wall time per stage of the ingest: handler stages (evidence_write, pipeline, projections, ontology, total), pipeline steps (`step.<id>`) and bulk-write phases (`bulk.<phase>`). |
| `observation_date_source` | `str` | Where the observation date the facts were anchored to came from: "caller" \| "request_time" \| "" (none — undated rows). |
| `under_operator_policy` | `bool` | True when the extraction ran under an operator's extraction policy; false on a deferred request. |
| `extract_prompt_keys` | `list[str]` | The sha256 keys of the rendered extractor prompts (one per segment; the exact-prompt cache's own key, no text) and the cache's hit / miss counts over this extraction's calls (0 / 0 = cache off). |
| `llm_cache_hits` | `int` | Extraction calls answered from the exact-prompt response cache. |
| `llm_cache_misses` | `int` | Extraction calls the cache could not answer. |

## `memory.stack`

Compose a token-budgeted recall bundle for agent wake-up.

`POST /v1/memory.stack` · MCP `loom_memory_stack` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | required | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `token_budget` | `int` | `4000` | Estimated tokens (chars / 4) all sections share; an entry that would overflow it ends its section. |
| `pinned_limit` | `int` | `10` | At most this many pinned memories, newest version first (0 skips the section). |
| `recent_limit` | `int` | `20` | At most this many recalled, unpinned memories, most recalled first (0 skips the section). |

| `seed_query` | `str` | `''` | Drives the procedure.match query and the knowledge-search query. |
| `procedure_limit` | `int` | `3` | Procedures to match on `seed_query`; 0, or no `seed_query`, skips the section. |

| --- | --- | --- |
| `entries` | `list[_StackEntry]` | Profile, pinned, recent_recall, procedure, knowledge entries, in that section order. |
| `tokens_used` | `int` | Estimated tokens the returned entries use (chars / 4 each). |
| `tokens_budget` | `int` | The `token_budget` the bundle was trimmed to, echoed. |
| `truncated` | `bool` | true when at least one section was trimmed to fit |
| `section_counts` | `dict[str, int]` | how many entries per section |

## `memory.touch`

Change only a memory's expiry: set a new TTL (`ttl_seconds`) or clear it (`clear_expiry`), for one key or up to 1,000 (`memory_keys`), without rewriting its value, entities, conflict state or…

`POST /v1/memory.touch` · MCP `loom_memory_touch` · role `writer` · write · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | required | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The agent run (task scope) the call belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | `''` | One key to touch; send it or `memory_keys`, not both. |
| `memory_keys` | `list[str]` | *(computed)* | Many keys of the same identity in one call — one read, one loom.memory insert, one batched embedding re-emit. |
| `ttl_seconds` | `int \| None` | `None` | New expiry this many seconds from now; send it or `clear_expiry: true`, not both. |
| `clear_expiry` | `bool` | `False` | "never expire" — expires_at becomes NULL. |
| `on_expire` | `Literal['', 'tombstone', 'demote', 'anonymize']` | `''` | Optionally re-declare the post-action alongside the new expiry. |
| `expire_reason` | `str` | `''` | Why the new expiry is set (at most 512 chars, not starting with `blacklist.sweep:`); '' keeps the row's reason. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `touched` | `bool` | single key: False when it doesn't exist; many: any touched |
| `version` | `int \| None` | Single key: the new version (None when not touched). |
| `expires_at` | `datetime \| None` | The new expiry of the touched rows; None when cleared or none touched. |
| `results` | `list[MemoryTouchResult]` | With `memory_keys`, one row per asked key. |
| `touched_count` | `int` | With `memory_keys`, how many keys were touched; 0 for one key. |

## `memory.update`

Key-addressed update: the fact changed or got more specific.

`POST /v1/memory.update` · MCP `loom_memory_update` · role `writer` · write · audited

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `namespace` | `str` | required | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | required | The key to update, resolved across the namespace unless an identity field below narrows it. |
| `value` | `dict[str, Any] \| list[Any] \| str \| int \| float \| bool \| None` | `None` | None = keep the current value (a tags/concepts-only rewrite). |
| `agent` | `str` | `''` | Narrows the key to rows written by this agent; "", "-" or "*" = any agent. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `''` | Narrows the key to this user's rows; "" or "-" = any user. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `''` | Narrows the key to this session's rows; "" or "-" = any session. |
| `run_id` | `str` | `''` | The run this revision is made under: stamped on the new version's row so the run ledger and the `acted` fold see that this run rewrote the key. |
| `tags` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | Replace the row's tags (lowercased); None keeps them, [] clears them. |
| `concepts` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | Replace the row's code concepts (symbol, library and error names); None keeps them. |
| `confidence` | `float \| None` | `None` | New confidence for the written version (None = keep the row's). |
| `reason` | `str` | `''` | Why the fact changed — lands in the audit row (audit=True), not on the memory. |
| `if_match_sha256` | `str` | `''` | Content hash the live row must still carry, else 409 PRECONDITION_FAILED; '' skips the check. |
| `char_limit` | `int \| None` | `None` | Char cap on the new value (422 on exceed); None = no cap on the new version, so pass the row's cap back to keep it. |
| `revive` | `bool` | `False` | Allow updating an expired row (else 409 EXPIRED); the update clears its expiry. |
| `relations` | `list[tuple[str, str, str]]` | *(computed)* | The facts the new value states, as MemorySetInput.relations; [] states none. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `updated` | `bool` | True when a new version was written; False with `reason` otherwise. |
| `memory_id` | `str` | Stable id of the updated row; '' when not found. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | The row's key (the asked key when not found). |
| `new_version` | `int` | Nanosecond version of the written row; 0 when nothing was written. |
| `content_sha256` | `str` | SHA-256 of the new value; send it as `if_match_sha256` on the next write. |
| `reason` | `str` | "" on success; "not_found" when no live row carries the key. |
| `candidates` | `list[MemoryUpdateCandidate]` | Filled only when the key resolved to several rows (also in the 409 detail). |
| `conflict_verdict` | `str` | See MemoryUpdateByIdOutput. |
| `conflict_peers` | `int` | How many existing rows the conflict check matched the new value to. |
| `duplicate_of` | `str` | memory_id of the row the new value restates, when the check found one. |

## `memory.verify`

Attest to (or revoke the attestation on) one memory.

`POST /v1/memory.verify` · MCP `loom_memory_verify` · role `writer` · idempotent · audited

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `memory_id` | `str` | `''` | The row to attest, by id; '' = address it by `namespace` + `memory_key`. |
| `namespace` | `str` | `''` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `agent` | `str` | `'-'` | The writing or reading agent; `'-'` or `'*'` means any agent where the op allows it. |
| `user_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The end user the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `session_id` | `str` | `'-'` | The session or conversation the row belongs to; `'-'` for none. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | `''` | With `namespace` and the writer identity, the row to attest when no `memory_id` is sent. |
| `revoke` | `bool` | `False` | True clears the attestation instead of making one. |
| `actor` | `str` | `''` | Attester recorded when the server runs without auth (`human:` / `process:` + subject); under auth the token decides. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `found` | `bool` | False when the row does not exist or the caller cannot write its namespace. |
| `changed` | `bool` | False when the call was a no-op (already attested by this actor and unchanged, or revoking a row with no attestation). |
| `memory_id` | `str` | Stable id of the attested row; '' when not found. |
| `memory_key` | `str` | The row's key; '' when not found. |
| `namespace` | `str` | The namespace the op reads or writes. |
| `verified_by` | `str` | The attester now on the row; '' after a revoke. |
| `verified_at` | `datetime \| None` | When the attestation was made; None after a revoke. |
| `verification` | `str` | State against the live content hash: human \| process \| stale \| none. |
| `version` | `int` | Version of the row after the call (the new row's when `changed`). |
| `content_sha256` | `str` | Canonical hash the attestation is bound to (== the row's live hash). |
